description: HUMAN-ONLY. Accept a committed as-built extraction for fabrication use (field-verified tie-in): recorded only when the signature verifies against the signing port. An agent always gets SCN_HUMAN_GATE with the document unchanged: hand it to the reviewer.

signature.description: Human signature object over the extraction payload; agents cannot produce one.

name: accept_asbuilt_extraction

description: HUMAN-ONLY. Accept a registration record for fabrication use (AF-34a): recorded only when the signature verifies against the signing port. An agent has no signature and always gets SCN_HUMAN_GATE with the document unchanged: hand the record to a reviewer.

signature.description: Human signature object from the signing system over the record payload; agents cannot produce one.

name: accept_registration

description: Apply a named configuration to the document: set each parameter listed in the configuration to its expression value, re-evaluate the parameter table in topological order, then replay featureHistory so all =expr geometry regenerates with the variant's values. Use after create_configuration to switch between model variants (e.g. "small" vs "large"). The configuration must already exist in the document (call create_configuration first).

name.description: Name of the configuration to activate. Must match an existing configuration created by create_configuration (case-sensitive). Example: "small", "large", "production_v2".

name: activate_configuration

description: Create a road / channel alignment from points of intersection (PIs, document units). Each interior PI can carry a simple circular curve of the given radius (0 = sharp corner). Draws the centreline, station ticks labelled km+mmm.mm every `stationInterval`, and PC / PT / R labels. Optional `spirals` adds a symmetric clothoid transition (TS-SC ... CS-ST, length Ls each side) per curved PI; the deflection must be at least twice the spiral angle Ls / (2 R). Add a design profile with set_alignment_profile and a road template with set_road_section to get the corridor, batters to daylight and earthworks; report with alignment_report.

points.description: PIs from start to end, at least 2: [[x, y], ...].

items.description: Point of intersection [x, y] in document units.

radii.description: Curve radius per interior PI (length = points - 2); 0 = no curve. Default all 0.

spirals.description: Clothoid length on each side of the circular curve per interior PI (length = points - 2); 0 = no spiral; needs radius > 0. Default all 0.

startStation.description: Station of the first point, document units. Default 0.

stationInterval.description: Station tick / section spacing (> 0). Default 20 m.

name: add_alignment

description: Append a step to a nonlinear_static analysis (needs set_nonlinear_controls first). Each step has step time 1 and is one CalculiX *STEP with *STATIC automatic incrementation. multipliers: factor per LOAD CASE (the loadCase of add_fea_load) reached at the END of the step, ramped from the previous value; a load case you leave out keeps its previous value (0 in the first step), 0 removes it, so load -> unload -> reload is three steps. amplitude: "ramp" (default, linear over the step) or "step" (full value from the first increment). control.kind "load": loads ramp, with increments { initialIncrement, minIncrement, maxIncrement, maxIncrements } as fractions of the step time. control.kind "displacement": also prescribes target (faces/points) + dof + value (document length units, at the end of the step); use it to trace past a load peak (limit load of a perfectly plastic part). "arc_length" is refused: CalculiX has no Riks procedure. Returns the step id in affected[0].

amplitude.description: "ramp" (default) or "step" (full multiplier from the first increment).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

anyOf.description: Load control: the load-case multipliers of the step ramp up over the step.

initialIncrement.description: First increment as a fraction of the step time (step time = 1), > 0, e.g. 0.05.

maxIncrement.description: Largest increment, fraction of the step time, >= initialIncrement and <= 1.

maxIncrements.description: Most increments the step may take (*STEP INC); the run stops with an error when reached. >= 1.

minIncrement.description: Smallest increment the solver may cut back to, fraction of the step time, > 0, <= initialIncrement.

anyOf.description: Displacement control: prescribes the target displacement (it can follow a load peak, load control cannot).

initialIncrement.description: First increment as a fraction of the step time (step time = 1), > 0, e.g. 0.05.

maxIncrement.description: Largest increment, fraction of the step time, >= initialIncrement and <= 1.

maxIncrements.description: Most increments the step may take (*STEP INC); the run stops with an error when reached. >= 1.

minIncrement.description: Smallest increment the solver may cut back to, fraction of the step time, > 0, <= initialIncrement.

target.description: Faces / edges / points whose nodes are driven (usually a loaded face).

edgesNear.description: Points identifying edges: each resolves to the nearest edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended edge.

entityId.description: Id of the analysed 3D entity (it must be a part of the analysis: set_part_idealization).

facesNear.description: Points identifying faces: each resolves to the NEAREST face of the entity at meshing time.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended face.

intersectPlane.description: Optional: restrict the target to the curve where the faces meet this plane.

normal.description: Plane normal (need not be unit length).

pointsNear.description: Points identifying vertices / locations: each resolves to the nearest vertex or node.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended vertex or location.

value.description: Displacement of the target nodes at the END of the step, in DOCUMENT length units (signed); ramps from the previous step value.

anyOf.description: Arc-length (Riks) control: REFUSED, CalculiX has no such procedure.

initialArcLength.description: Initial arc length (not available on CalculiX).

maxSteps.description: Maximum arc-length steps (not available on CalculiX).

control.description: How the step is driven: { kind: "load", ...increments } or { kind: "displacement", target, dof, value, ...increments } (arc_length is refused).

multipliers.description: Load-case name -> multiplier on the load values at the END of the step (e.g. { LC1: 166 }); {} = no load change.

name.description: Display name of the step, e.g. "push" or "unload".

name: add_analysis_step

description: Add steel base plates with anchor bolts under steel columns (the given memberIds, or every steel column of the level that has none yet). Plate = column profile + margin on each side; follows its column when it moves and is deleted / copied with it. Plate mass and bolt counts feed the takeoff.

boltDiameter.description: Bolt diameter, in document units. Default 24 mm (M24).

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level.

margin.description: Plate overhang beyond the profile, in document units. Default 100 mm.

memberIds.description: Steel column ids. Default: every unplated steel column of the level.

thickness.description: Plate thickness, in document units. Default 25 mm (20 mm for profiles < 300 deep).

name: add_base_plates

description: Add a stiffening bead (a formed rib of circular cross-section) along a straight path on ONE flat of a sheet-metal part. The flat is picked by the world point `face.near`; `path` is [start, end], two world points [x, y, z] projected onto the flat plane. radius is the INSIDE radius of the arch (groove side), depth the height of the bead crown above the flat face on the bead side (0 < depth < radius), both in the document length unit; the arch is T thick (outer radius = radius + T). endShape 'round' closes both ends with a revolved cap (footprint = capsule); 'open' leaves the arch open at both path ends. The cross-section has no blend radii (junctions on the radial rays). The bead stays wholly inside the flat, clear of its edges, bends, cutouts and other beads. The flat pattern is NOT changed: the bead is excluded and listed as a forming note (flat_pattern data.formingNotes, DXF NOTES); the blank is not adjusted for material drawn into the bead. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FORM_INVALID, FTR_CUTOUT_INVALID. Next: flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

depth.description: Height of the bead crown above the flat face on the bead side, in the document length unit; 0 < depth < radius.

direction.description: Bead towards the flat's +normal face ('up', default) or the -normal face ('down').

endShape.description: End treatment: 'round' (closed revolved caps) or 'open' (arch open at both ends).

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or near the flat that gets the bead (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

path.description: Straight bead centre line as two world points, projected onto the picked flat (document length unit).

items.description: Bead start [x, y, z], world point (document length unit).

radius.description: Inside radius of the bead arch in the document length unit; > depth.

name: add_bead

description: Add a horizontal beam from start to end (plan [x, y]). Its top sits at the datum + topOffset; reference "levelTop" (default) = top of the level (elevation + level height), i.e. under the next floor slab; "ffl" = level elevation. Refused if a beam over the same span (either direction) at the same topOffset already exists on the level.

depth.description: Section depth, in document units. Default 500 mm.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

reference.description: Datum of topOffset: "levelTop" = level elevation + level height (underside of the next floor), "ffl" = level finished floor elevation. The same reference and topOffset put add_beam and add_grid_beams at the same absolute elevation. Default differs by domain and is kept so existing documents replay unchanged: add_beam "levelTop" (concrete beam under the next slab), add_grid_beams "ffl" (steel framing referenced to finished floor). Pass reference explicitly to be unambiguous; the summary states the resolved elevation.

topOffset.description: Offset of the beam top from the datum chosen by reference, in document units. Default 0.

width.description: Section width, in document units. Default 300 mm.

name: add_beam

description: Create a simplified rolling bearing: an inner ring and an outer ring (revolved raceway sections) plus a ring of rolling elements (balls for deep_groove_ball; straight rollers for spherical_roller / cylindrical_roller; rollers tilted 12 degrees for tapered_roller), all grouped under one named group (group_entities semantics). Size it with designation (ISO 15 boundary dimensions in MILLIMETRES, converted to the document units; case/space-insensitive, a suffix after "-" is ignored; known: 60xx/62xx/63xx deep groove e.g. "6205", 222xx spherical roller e.g. "22220", 302xx tapered roller e.g. "30210", NU2xx/NU3xx cylindrical roller e.g. "NU210") OR explicit bore, outerDiameter, width in document units (type then defaults to deep_groove_ball). An unknown designation, or a type that contradicts the designation, is rejected. The bearing is centered on position with its rotation axis along axis (default +Z). Returns affected = [inner ring, outer ring, ...rolling elements, group id] and data {groupId, innerRingId, outerRingId, rollingElementIds, type, bore, outerDiameter, width, designation?}.

axis.description: Rotation axis direction [dx, dy, dz] (non-zero, normalized) of the bearing. Defaults to [0, 0, 1].

bore.description: Bore (inner diameter) in document units. Needed with outerDiameter and width when no designation.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#b0b6bf".

designation.description: Bearing designation, e.g. "6205", "22220", "30210", "NU210". Dimensions in mm, scaled to document units.

outerDiameter.description: Outer diameter in document units. Must exceed bore by >= 20% of itself.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Center of the bearing (mid-width on its axis). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

type.description: Bearing type. Optional when designation is given (inferred); must match it if both are given.

width.description: Bearing width along the axis in document units.

name: add_bearing

description: Create a straight bevel gear with real involute-style teeth as ONE closed mesh solid (no booleans). The pitch cone is derived from teeth, matingTeeth and shaftAngle (90° default): pitchAngle = atan(sin(shaft)/(matingTeeth/teeth + cos(shaft))); or pass pitchAngle explicitly. Heel (large end) face lies at the local z = 0 plane centred on `position`; the tooth profile is the module*teeth/2 pitch-circle spur outline and shrinks linearly towards the cone apex, which lies on the axis at +axis side (apex height = coneDistance*cos(pitchAngle)). `axis` selects the world direction of the gear axis (apex side), `rotation` is then applied about `position`. Tooth form is approximate (no Tredgold back-cone correction). `bore` cuts a cylindrical through hole. For two meshing gears use add_bevel_gear_pair. Result is a world-space mesh entity.

axis.description: World direction of the gear axis (towards the apex). Default "z".

bore.description: Radius of a central through hole, >= 0. Default 0 (solid).

color.description: Hex color. Default "#b08d57".

faceWidth.description: Tooth length along the cone element (heel to toe), > 0 and <= 0.7 * cone distance; usual practice <= cone distance / 3.

matingTeeth.description: Tooth count of the mating gear, integer >= 6. Default: same as teeth (miter gear).

module.description: Gear module (metric) at the heel (large end), > 0.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

pitchAngle.description: Pitch-cone half angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Overrides the value derived from the tooth counts.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the heel face. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Pressure angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Default 0.3491 (20°).

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Applied about `position` after `axis`.  Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

shaftAngle.description: Angle between the two shaft axes in RADIANS, in (0, π). Default π/2 (90°).

teeth.description: Tooth count of THIS gear, integer >= 6.

toothPhase.description: Rotation of the tooth pattern about the gear axis in RADIANS. Default 0 (tooth 0 centred on +X).

name: add_bevel_gear

description: Create a meshing pair of straight bevel gears at a 90° shaft angle: a pinion (axis along world Z) and a wheel (axis along world X) whose pitch-cone apexes coincide at `position` (the cone apex, default origin). The pinion heel face lies at z = apex - apexHeight, the wheel heel face at x = apex - apexHeight; teeth are phased so they mesh with backlash. Pitch angles: pinion atan(pinionTeeth/wheelTeeth), wheel 90° minus that. Returns affected = [pinion, wheel] and data {ratio, pinionPitchAngle, wheelPitchAngle, coneDistance}.

faceWidth.description: Tooth length along the cone element (heel to toe), > 0 and <= 0.7 * cone distance; usual practice <= cone distance / 3.

module.description: Gear module (metric) at the heel (large end), > 0.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. This is the common cone apex. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Pressure angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Default 0.3491 (20°).

name: add_bevel_gear_pair

description: Connect a rigid body (child) to the ground or to another body (parent), for simulate_motion. "revolute": the child spins about `axis` through `anchor` (a shaft in its bearings, a propeller hub, a crank pin, a hinge). "prismatic": the child slides along `axis` (a piston in its bore). "spherical": a ball pin at `anchor` (three rotations); it can only CLOSE A LOOP, never be the only connection of a body. `anchor` is a world point on the axis in DOCUMENT units (e.g. the shaft centre); `axis` a world direction (need not be unit; not used by spherical). A body may be the child of SEVERAL joints: that makes a closed loop (slider-crank, four-bar, multi-cylinder engine). llull then picks the spanning tree itself (prismatic joints first, then revolute, in creation order, so the last-declared joint of a loop becomes the closing constraint) and reports it in inspect_dynamics (data.topology, data.mobility: degrees of freedom, redundant constraints). Loop joints have no coordinate of their own: motors, gears, propellers and cylinder pressure must sit on tree joints. In a planar loop make one revolute loop joint "spherical" to avoid redundant constraints. Refusals: FPR_LOOP_PRISMATIC (a prismatic joint would close a loop: re-order, or use a revolute joint there), FPR_SPHERICAL_TREE (reported by inspect_dynamics / simulate_motion while a spherical joint is the only connection of its body: declare the revolute or prismatic joint too, in any order). The loop must be closed at the start pose: every joint has one anchor, so the pose of the bodies is the pose you modelled; give `anchorOnChild` only to state where the pin sits on the child body when it differs (the distance is the loop gap; above 1 µm simulate_motion refuses with FPR_LOOP_OPEN). Optional: damping (viscous, N·m·s/rad), friction (dry, N·m), initialRpm / initialVelocity (speed at t = 0). SPRING: `stiffness` makes the joint a spring (torsional N·m/rad for revolute, linear N/m for prismatic; 1 N/mm = 1000 N/m, 1 N·m/deg = 57.2958 N·m/rad) that is relaxed at `springReference` (rad or m, measured from the pose the joint is modelled in; default 0 = relaxed at the start pose). Mass-spring: prismatic joint + stiffness k, period 2π·sqrt(m/k). Spring energy counts in the potential energy of simulate_motion (energy: true). A spring needs a tree joint (not a loop-closing one). Returns the joint id in affected[0].

anchor.description: World point on the joint axis (the pin centre for spherical), document units, e.g. the shaft centre [0, 200, 800].

anchorOnChild.description: Where the pin sits on the child body, document units, when it differs from anchor. Only used when the joint closes a loop: the distance to anchor is the loop gap (refused above 1 µm). Default = anchor.

axis.description: World direction of the axis, e.g. [0, 1, 0] for a shaft along Y. Required for revolute and prismatic.

damping.description: Viscous damping: N·m·s/rad (revolute) or N·s/m (prismatic). Default 0.

friction.description: Dry friction: N·m (revolute) or N (prismatic). Default 0.

id.description: Optional explicit joint id.

initialRpm.description: Revolute only: speed at t = 0 in rpm (overrides initialVelocity).

initialVelocity.description: Speed at t = 0: rad/s (revolute) or m/s (prismatic). Default 0.

kind.description: "revolute" = rotation about the axis; "prismatic" = translation along it; "spherical" = ball pin, loop closure only.

parent.description: Body the child is mounted on, or "ground" (default) for the fixed world.

springReference.description: Joint coordinate where the spring is relaxed: rad (revolute) or metres (prismatic), measured from the pose the joint is modelled in. Default 0.

stiffness.description: Spring stiffness: N·m/rad (revolute) or N/m (prismatic; 1 N/mm = 1000 N/m). Default 0 = no spring. Not for spherical.

name: add_body_joint

description: Create a rectangular box solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. size is [width, height, depth] in document units; all components must be > 0. anchor controls which point on the entity the position refers to: "center" (default) = geometric center; "min" = min-XYZ corner; "base-center" = center of bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin.

anchor.description: Which point on the box the position refers to. "center" (default): geometric center. "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

size.description: [width, height, depth] in document units. All three components must be > 0.

name: add_box

description: Create a complete starter building to edit or learn from: "house" (two-storey 10 × 8 m house: grid, masonry walls, partition, doors, windows, slabs, stair, rooms, roof) or "office" (three-storey 22.5 × 12.5 m concrete frame: grid, columns at intersections, beams, façade openings, slabs, stair, rooms, roof). The camera is framed on the result. All-or-nothing: the document is unchanged if any step fails.
name: add_building_template

description: Route a cable tray (open U section) through 3D points [[x, y, z], …] (z = tray centre above the level) with a width, side height and cable system (power, data, instrumentation…). Lengths feed the takeoff; clashes with steel, pipes and equipment are reported by check_clashes. Refused if a tray of the same size already follows the same route (either direction) on the level.

height.description: Side height, in document units. Default 60 mm.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

points.description: Tray centreline [[x, y, z], …], 2 to 1000 points.

width.description: Tray width, in document units. Default 300 mm.

name: add_cable_tray

description: Group faces into a radiation cavity of a heat_* analysis (CalculiX *RADIATE, CAVITY with view factors computed by the solver); returns the cavity id in affected[0]. name: 1-3 letters, digits or underscores, unique. faces: at least 2 { target (facesNear), emissivity 0-1 }. environmentTemperature { value, unit } makes the cavity OPEN (the remainder radiates to that temperature); omit it for a CLOSED cavity (view factors scaled to 1). Check the geometry first with compute_view_factors. Radiation is evaluated on absolute temperature.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

environmentTemperature.description: Open cavity: temperature { value, unit } the unclosed part of the view radiates to. Omit for a closed cavity.

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

emissivity.description: Hemispherical emissivity of these faces, 0 to 1.

target.description: Radiating faces of a part (facesNear points).

edgesNear.description: Points identifying edges: each resolves to the nearest edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended edge.

entityId.description: Id of the analysed 3D entity (it must be a part of the analysis: set_part_idealization).

facesNear.description: Points identifying faces: each resolves to the NEAREST face of the entity at meshing time.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended face.

intersectPlane.description: Optional: restrict the target to the curve where the faces meet this plane.

normal.description: Plane normal (need not be unit length).

pointsNear.description: Points identifying vertices / locations: each resolves to the nearest vertex or node.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended vertex or location.

name.description: Cavity name, 1-3 letters, digits or underscores (CalculiX limit), unique in the analysis, e.g. "C1".

name: add_cavity_radiation

description: Add a structural column standing on a level, at a plan location or (atGridIntersections: true) at every structural grid intersection. Rectangular width × depth, or circular with diameter = width. Locations that already hold a column on the level are skipped (listed in the summary); refused when all are occupied.

atGridIntersections.description: Place one column at every grid-axis intersection instead of at location.

depth.description: Section depth (rectangular), in document units. Default = width.

height.description: Column height, in document units. Default: the level height.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

width.description: Section width (diameter if circular), in document units. Default 300 mm.

name: add_column

description: Create a cone solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. radius and height must both be > 0. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "base-center" (default) = center of the circular base (the apex is at position + [0,0,height]); "center" = geometric center of the AABB; "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB. The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin. Orientation: pass EITHER rotation (Euler radians) OR axis [dx,dy,dz] = direction the local +Z (symmetry) axis should point in world space; axis wins when both are given and Euler angles are derived and stored.

anchor.description: Which point on the cone the position refers to. "base-center" (default): center of the circular base; apex at position+[0,0,height]. "center": geometric center of the AABB (mid X/Y/Z). "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. Unknown values fall back to "base-center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

axis.description: Optional direction [dx, dy, dz] (any non-zero length, normalized) that the primitive local +Z axis (its symmetry axis) points along in world space, e.g. [1, 0, 0] lays it along +X. When given it OVERRIDES rotation (the rotation param is ignored and the resolved Euler angles are stored). A zero-length or malformed axis is rejected as a no-op.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

height.description: Height from the base center to the apex along the local +Z axis in document units. Must be > 0.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Radius of the circular base in document units. Must be > 0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_cone

description: Add a geometric or dimensional constraint between two entity references. Geometric kinds (coincident, parallel, perpendicular, tangent) impose a positional or directional relationship with no numeric target. Dimensional kinds (distance, angle) require a numeric "value" field. Call solve_constraints afterward to update entity positions. Returns the new constraint id in affected[0].

constraint.description: The constraint to add. Must have: "kind" (one of coincident|parallel|perpendicular|tangent|distance|angle), "a" (EntityRef: { entityId: string, kind?: "start"|"end"|"center"|"mid" }), "b" (EntityRef: same shape). Dimensional kinds also require "value": a number or parameter expression string.

a.description: First entity reference. Minimum: { entityId: "<id>" }. Optional sub-point: { entityId: "<id>", kind: "start"|"end"|"center"|"mid" } to target a specific geometric point on a line, arc, or circle.

entityId.description: Id of the first entity.

kind.description: Sub-point selector: start, end, center, or mid.

b.description: Second entity reference. Same shape as "a". { entityId: "<id>" } or { entityId: "<id>", kind: "start"|"end"|"center"|"mid" }.

entityId.description: Id of the second entity.

kind.description: Sub-point selector: start, end, center, or mid.

Constraint type. Geometric: "coincident" (two points share a location), "parallel" (two lines are parallel), "perpendicular" (two lines are at 90°), "tangent" (line tangent to circle/arc, or two arcs externally tangent). Dimensional: "distance" (distance between two points equals value), "angle" (angle between two line directions equals value in radians).

value.description: Required for dimensional constraints (distance, angle). A numeric literal ("10", "1.5708") or a parameter expression string ("width", "height / 2"). Angle is in radians.

id.description: Optional explicit constraint id. When omitted a unique id is generated. If the id already exists in the document the command is a no-op.

name: add_constraint

description: Add a contour flange to a sheet-metal part: an open profile of straight legs joined by bends of one inside radius, swept along a straight edge picked by `edge.near` (Z, channel, hat, stepped lips). path lists the profile vertices P1..Pn as [u, v] relative to the first mold vertex P0: u runs away from the edge in the base plane, v along the base +normal (document length unit). Every vertex of P0..P(n-1) becomes a bend of the turning angle there (a left turn bends up, a right turn bends down); the picked edge is the tangent line of the first bend, so the first segment must leave the base plane (v != 0 direction). side says which sheet face the path follows: 'top' (the +normal face, inside of up bends), 'bottom', or 'mid' (mid-thickness); setbacks are tan(angle/2) x (R, R+T or R+T/2) accordingly and the legs are the segments minus their setbacks. All joins are tangent arcs of insideRadius (default the rule radius). widthStart / widthEnd inset the flange from the edge ends (document length unit). The flat pattern is analytic (BA = angle x (R + K T) per bend). Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_BEND_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_BEND_RADIUS_BELOW_MIN, FTR_SHARP_BEND_FORBIDDEN, FTR_FLANGE_TOO_SHORT, FTR_EDGE_NOT_STRAIGHT, FTR_EDGE_OCCUPIED. Next: flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

edge.description: Edge selector (the tangent line of the first bend).

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or within one thickness of the straight edge that receives the flange (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

insideRadius.description: Inside radius of every bend in the document length unit; default the rule radius; >= 0.

path.description: Vertices P1..Pn of the profile, in order from the edge; the first segment P0 -> P1 must not lie in the base plane.

items.description: Profile vertex [u, v] relative to P0 in the document length unit: u away from the edge in the base plane, v along the base +normal.

side.description: Sheet face the path follows: 'top' (+normal face of the base), 'bottom' or 'mid' (mid-thickness).

widthEnd.description: Inset of the flange from the edge end, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

widthStart.description: Inset of the flange from the edge start, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

name: add_contour_flange

description: Cut a square corner relief into a flat of a sheet-metal part, at one right-angle outline corner (typically where two flanges meet and their bends stop short of the corner), so the flanges can form without tearing. The corner is picked by the world point `corner.near` (within one thickness of the flat corner vertex, which must be a convex 90-degree vertex). The notch removes a size x size square at the corner; size is in the document length unit and defaults to the rule radius + thickness + the rule relief depthExtra (returned as a named default in data.size). The notch must leave both adjacent edges longer than size and touch no bend line or cutout. The flat pattern loses the same square. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_RELIEF_INVALID. Next: check_sheet_metal, flat_pattern.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or within one thickness of the flat corner vertex to relieve (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

size.description: Side of the square notch in the document length unit; > 0. Default: rule inside radius + thickness + rule relief depthExtra (named default in the result).

name: add_corner_relief

description: Add an overhead-crane runway: crane beams along a plan line with their top at railHeight, split at supports every supportSpacing, each support carried by a bracket cantilevered from the nearest steel column (within 2 m). Capacity (t) is noted on the members for schedules.

capacity.description: Crane capacity in tonnes (for notes). Default 10.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

railHeight.description: Top of the runway beam above the level, in document units (> 0).

supportSpacing.description: Distance between supports, in document units (> 0). Default 6000 mm.

name: add_crane_runway

description: Record a load-displacement curve of a nonlinear_static analysis: one point per stored increment (see set_nonlinear_controls outputIncrements), read from the CalculiX .dat output. load is either { kind: "load", loadId } (the multiplied value of that load at each increment) or { kind: "reaction", constraintId, component } (summed reaction force of the constraint nodes, component x | y | z | magnitude, as printed by CalculiX). loadId / constraintId accept the id or the unique name. displacement: { point, dof } reads ux | uy | uz | magnitude at the mesh node nearest to the point (document units, an exact node is not required). The curve starts at (0, 0). Returns the probe id in affected[0]; the solved summary lists points, peak load and displacement range per probe.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

displacement.description: What is plotted on the displacement axis.

point.description: Location [x, y, z] in document units; the nearest mesh node is read.

kind.description: Load axis is the multiplied value of one load.

loadId.description: Id (or unique name) of a load of this analysis; the curve uses magnitude x step multiplier.

component.description: Reaction force component in the global axes, or its magnitude.

constraintId.description: Id (or unique name) of a constraint of this analysis; its nodes carry the reaction.

kind.description: Load axis is the reaction force summed over the nodes of one constraint.

load.description: What is plotted on the load axis.

name.description: Display name of the curve, e.g. "tip".

name: add_curve_probe

description: Add a curved (arc) wall on a level: its centreline is the circular arc from start through a point on the arc to end (all [x, y]). Thickness, height (default: level height), base offset and material as for draw_walls. Counted with the walls in quantities and schedules. Hosts doors and windows (add_door / add_window with its id; offset = distance along the arc). Refused if the same arc (either direction) and base offset already exists on the level.

height.description: Wall height. Default: the level height.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

thickness.description: Wall thickness, in document units. Default 200 mm.

through.description: Any point on the arc between start and end [x, y] (sets the curvature).

name: add_curved_wall

description: Create a cylinder solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. radius and height must both be > 0. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "center" (default) = geometric center (cylinder spans ±height/2 about stored position along its axis); "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB; "base-center" = center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z of AABB). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin. Orientation: pass EITHER rotation (Euler radians) OR axis [dx,dy,dz] = direction the local +Z (symmetry) axis should point in world space; axis wins when both are given and Euler angles are derived and stored.

anchor.description: Which point on the cylinder the position refers to. "center" (default): geometric center. "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

axis.description: Optional direction [dx, dy, dz] (any non-zero length, normalized) that the primitive local +Z axis (its symmetry axis) points along in world space, e.g. [1, 0, 0] lays it along +X. When given it OVERRIDES rotation (the rotation param is ignored and the resolved Euler angles are stored). A zero-length or malformed axis is rejected as a no-op.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

height.description: Total height of the cylinder in document units. Must be > 0.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Radius of the cylinder cross-section in document units. Must be > 0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_cylinder

description: Gas pressure on a piston, for simulate_motion: force = (p - ambient) x bore area pushes the piston toward the crank, applied as the generalised force of the prismatic joint `piston` (the cylinder body gets the reaction). The crank joint gives the crank angle. Needs the slider-crank joints already declared (crank revolute to ground, rod revolute on the crank, wrist pin revolute or spherical rod-to-piston, piston prismatic): crank radius, rod length, cylinder axis and the crank angle of the top dead centre (TDC) are read from their anchors at t = 0 (set tdcCrankAngleDeg to override). Units: bore mm; pressures Pa (1 bar = 1e5 Pa); angles deg; heat J per cycle per cylinder. cycle "four_stroke" (default, 720 deg) or "two_stroke" (360). Cycle angle 0 = firing TDC, intake 360-540, compression 540-720, power 0-180, exhaust 180-360. firingOffsetDeg: which TDC crossing of this piston fires, 0 or 360 (multi-cylinder firing order comes from the crank-pin phasing of the geometry plus this 0/360 choice). The crank must turn in the positive sense of its joint axis (flip the axis otherwise). Models: "table" = gauge pressure vs cycle angle (must cover the whole cycle, else FPR_PRESSURE_TABLE_GAP; give `source` or results are unverified). "wiebe" = single zone without heat loss: polytropic compression (n_c) and expansion (n_e) with a Wiebe heat release (startDeg, durationDeg, a, m; gasoline a 5, m 2), heat per cycle OR calibrated exactly to a net `target_imep_Pa` (FPR_IMEP_UNREACHABLE when it is below the unfired loop). n_c, n_e and intakePressurePa are required, no defaults. "single_zone" = first law with Wiebe burn (ca50Deg 8-10 for MBT, or fixed startDeg; durationDeg about 35 at 3000 rpm), Woschni wall heat loss (give all six `woschni` constants, or omit the object for 3.26 / 2.28 / 6.18 / 0.00324, exponent -0.53, wall 450 K, which are then stored), charge at intake closing (intakePressurePa, intakeTempK), heat per cycle or per rpm (calibration to a brake torque needs engine losses and is not available yet). Returns the cylinder id (cyl-<step>.<k>) in affected[0]; the summary gives geometry, peak pressure and IMEP. Next: simulate_motion (reactions peaks, data.engineReport), or engine_quick_check for a sanity check without simulation.

ambientPressurePa.description: Ambient pressure acting under the piston, Pa. Default 101325 (ISA sea level).

crank.description: Id of the revolute joint of the crankshaft (its angle is the engine angle).

firingOffsetDeg.description: Which TDC crossing fires: 0 (default) or 360 for a four-stroke.

id.description: Optional explicit cylinder id.

model.description: Pressure model; see the command description.

a.description: wiebe: Wiebe a (5 is typical for gasoline).
Wiebe efficiency parameter (5 is typical for gasoline).

ca50Deg.description: Crank angle of 50 % burned, deg after firing TDC (MBT is about 8-10). Give this OR startDeg.

durationDeg.description: Burn duration in crank degrees at 3000 rpm (about 35 for 0-90 % burn at medium speed); scaled by (rpm / 3000)^rpmExponent.

m.description: Wiebe form factor, > -1 (2 is typical for gasoline).

rpmExponent.description: Exponent of the burn-duration speed scaling. Default 0.2.

startDeg.description: Start of combustion, deg (negative = before firing TDC); a fixed spark. Give this OR ca50Deg.

compressionIndex.description: wiebe: polytropic index n_c of compression and burn, > 1 (about 1.3). Required, no default.

expansionIndex.description: wiebe: polytropic index n_e of expansion, > 1 (about 1.3). Required, no default.

heat.description: wiebe: per_cycle_J or target_imep_Pa. single_zone: per_cycle_J or table_vs_rpm (calibration to a brake target needs engine losses and is not offered yet).

kind.description: "per_cycle_J": heat released per cycle (wiebe, single_zone); "target_imep_Pa": calibrate to this net IMEP (wiebe only); "table_vs_rpm": heat per cycle vs rpm (single_zone only).

points.description: table_vs_rpm: [[rpm, joules per cycle], ...]; linear between points, flat outside.

value.description: per_cycle_J: joules per cycle per cylinder; target_imep_Pa: net indicated mean effective pressure in Pa (1 bar = 1e5 Pa).

intakePressurePa.description: wiebe, single_zone: absolute pressure at intake closing (bottom dead centre), Pa.

intakeTempK.description: single_zone: charge temperature at intake closing, K (e.g. 330).

m.description: wiebe: Wiebe m, > -1 (2 is typical for gasoline).

points.description: table: [[cycle angle deg, GAUGE pressure Pa], ...]; angle 0 = firing TDC, must cover 0..720 (four_stroke) or 0..360; periodic.

source.description: Where the pressure data or constants come from; without one the result is flagged unverified.

startDeg.description: wiebe: start of combustion, deg (negative = before firing TDC, e.g. -15).

woschni.description: single_zone: Woschni heat-transfer constants; missing ones take the stated defaults and are stored.

c2Closed.description: Gas-velocity coefficient with the valves closed (2.28).

c2Exchange.description: Gas-velocity coefficient during gas exchange (6.18); kept in the record, the exchange strokes are prescribed pressures.

tempExponent.description: Gas temperature exponent (-0.53; -0.55 in some sources).

piston.description: Id of the prismatic joint of the piston (add_body_joint kind prismatic).

tdcCrankAngleDeg.description: Crank joint angle (deg from its t = 0 pose) at which this piston is at TDC; default computed from the geometry.

name: add_cylinder_pressure

description: Paint a line of text onto a 3D solid as a decal (logo, brand, part number, sidewall lettering): it is projected along -normal onto the faces turned toward it within the decal box, keeps following the solid when it moves or rotates, shows in the viewport and is exported to glTF as a textured overlay (never part of STL / STEP solids). Text uses the built-in block font (A–Z, 0–9, - . , : / + & ! ? ' #; lower case prints as capitals). Place it with `at` (a world point on the surface) and `normal` (the outward surface direction there).

angle.description: Rotation of the text about the normal, radians (default 0).

at.description: World point on the surface at the decal centre.

background.description: Optional #rrggbb background behind the letters (default transparent).

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#ffffff".

depth.description: Projection depth through curved surfaces (> 0). Default: 2 × height.

height.description: Letter block height in document units (> 0).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid to paint.

normal.description: Outward surface direction at `at` (world); the decal projects along -normal.

width.description: Decal width (> 0). Default: from the text length at this height.

name: add_decal

description: Add a detail view to a drawing sheet: a circle on a parent (projection or section) view is drawn magnified and clipped to the circle, labelled "DETAIL B (2:1)" with the next free letter; the circle and letter are drawn on the parent. `center` and `radius` are in the parent view's projected model coordinates (document units; for a front view x = world X, y = world Z). Default scale is the standard scale at least 2x the sheet scale (1:10 sheet -> 1:5, 1:5 -> 1:2). Returns the view id.

center.description: Circle centre in the parent view's projected model coordinates (document units).

paperPosition.description: Centre of the detail on the paper in millimetres. Omit for automatic layout.

parentViewId.description: View (projection or section) the circle is on.

scale.description: Scale denominator N of the detail, e.g. 0.5 = 2:1. Omit for the standard scale at least 2x the sheet scale.

name: add_detail_view

description: Place an associative dimension annotation in the document and report the measured value in the summary. `dimensionKind` controls the measurement type: 'linear' — distance between 2 line or point entities, measured along X (horizontal) or along Y (vertical) whichever separation is larger, between their midpoints/positions (entityIds length=2); 'aligned' — true distance between 2 line or point entities, dimension line parallel to the segment joining them (entityIds length=2); 'radial' — radius of a circle, arc, or ellipse entity (entityIds length=1); 'diameter' — diameter of a circle, arc, or ellipse entity, drawn with a Ø prefix (entityIds length=1); 'angular' — minor angle in degrees: either 2 line entities (the vertex is the intersection of the two infinite lines; parallel lines are rejected) or 3 entities (vertex point first, then 2 line or point entities). `entityIds` is an array of existing entity ids whose geometry the dimension measures; the count must match the kind. Optional `offset` is the perpendicular distance (model units) from the measured geometry to the dimension line (default 5); for angular it is the arc radius, and for radial/diameter a value in (0, 2π) is the leader angle in radians (default 5 rad). Optional `precision` overrides the document display precision (decimal places) for this dimension. Optional `tolerance` is drawn after the computed value, e.g. '±0.1', '+0.05/-0.02' or 'H7'. Optional `label` replaces the computed value (and tolerance) with a custom string (e.g. 'REF' or '≈ 42 mm'). Optional `layer` is the target layer id.

dimensionKind.description: Type of dimension to create. Must be one of: 'linear' (2 ids), 'aligned' (2 ids), 'radial' (1 id: circle/arc/ellipse), 'diameter' (1 id: circle/arc/ellipse), 'angular' (2 line ids, or 3 ids: vertex point + 2 lines/points).

entityIds.description: Ids of the referenced document entities. Count must match the dimensionKind: linear/aligned=2, radial/diameter=1, angular=2 (lines) or 3 (vertex + 2). All ids must exist in the document.

label.description: Custom text to display instead of the computed value, e.g. 'REF' or '≈ 42 mm'. Omit to show the computed measurement.

layer.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

offset.description: Perpendicular distance (model units) from the measured geometry to the dimension line. Default: 5.

precision.description: Number of decimal places to display for this dimension, overriding the document displayPrecision. Must be an integer in [0, 20]. Omit to use the document default.

tolerance.description: Tolerance text drawn after the computed value, e.g. '±0.1', '+0.05/-0.02' or a fit like 'H7'. Ignored when `label` is set.

name: add_dimension

description: Insert a door into a wall: cuts the wall, adds the door leaf (3D) and its swing arc (plan). The summary warns when the opening overlaps a column in the wall line. Refused if it does not fit in the wall or overlaps another opening.

at.description: Alternative to offset: a plan point [x, y] projected onto the wall to place the opening center. Ignored when offset is given.

height.description: Opening height in document units (> 0). Default 2100 mm, limited to the wall height.

mark.description: Schedule mark, unique among doors. Default next Dn.

offset.description: Distance along the wall from its start to the opening CENTER, in document units (arc length on a curved wall). Takes precedence over at. Default: wall midpoint.

sillHeight.description: Height of the opening bottom above the wall base, in document units (>= 0). Default 0 mm.

swing.description: Hinge side looking from wall start to end. The door opens toward the wall’s left side. Default left.

wallId.description: Host wall element id: a straight ("wall-1") or curved ("curvedWall-1") wall.

width.description: Opening width in document units (> 0). Default 900 mm.

name: add_door

description: Couple two kinematic joints: driven_value = driver_value * ratio + offset. Models gear trains (ratio = gear_ratio), belt drives, cam followers, or any linear coupling. Example: two meshing gears with 2:1 ratio — set ratio=2. "driver" is the source joint id (its value propagates). "driven" is the target joint id (its value is computed from the driver). "ratio" is the multiplication factor (may be negative for direction reversal). "offset" is an optional additive phase or position offset (default 0). Cyclic couplings (A→B→A) are rejected with an explanatory summary. Returns the new drive relation id in affected[0].

driven.description: Id of the driven joint (receives motion). Must exist in doc.joints.

driver.description: Id of the driving joint (source of motion). Must exist in doc.joints.

id.description: Optional explicit drive relation id. When omitted a unique id is generated. If the id already exists in doc.driveRelations the command is a no-op.

offset.description: Optional additive offset applied after ratio multiplication. Default: 0.

ratio.description: Coupling ratio: driven = driver * ratio + offset. Use 1.0 for a direct coupling, 2.0 for a 2:1 gear-up, -1.0 to reverse direction.

name: add_drive_relation

description: Place a machine / process equipment on a level: name, plan centre, size [length, width, height], plan rotation (radians), maintenance clearance around the footprint (checked by check_clashes) and operating weight in kg (for floor loads). Optional `shape` makes it a cylindrical vessel (vertical or horizontal). Shown as a block / cylinder in 3D and with its clearance zone in plan. An explicit `mark` must be unique among equipment.

clearance.description: Maintenance / operating clearance around it, in document units. Default 800 mm.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

location.description: Footprint centre [x, y] (a trailing z is ignored).

mark.description: Equipment tag, unique among equipment (duplicates are refused). Default EQn.

shape.description: Shape: "box" (default), "vertical_vessel" (cylinder, axis along Z: size = [diameter, ignored, height]; the width is set equal to the diameter) or "horizontal_vessel" (cylinder, axis along its local x: size = [length, diameter, ignored]; the height is set equal to the diameter and the bottom rests on the level). Plans draw a vertical vessel as a circle.

size.description: Three numbers. box: [length (local x), width (local y), height], all > 0. vertical_vessel: [diameter, ignored, height]. horizontal_vessel: [length along local x, diameter, ignored].

name: add_equipment

description: Cut the floors around an equipment that passes through them (e.g. a 12 m desolventizer crossing two gratings): every slab whose top lies inside the equipment height and is solid under its footprint gets an opening = the equipment plan rectangle + margin. Clears the matching check_clashes hard clashes. A slab where the opening would not fit (outside the slab, touching another opening) is reported and left.

margin.description: Free gap around the footprint (toe plate / access), in document units; must be >= 0. Default: 300 mm converted to document units.

name: add_equipment_openings

description: Add a support to an analysis, returning the constraint id in affected[0]. kind: fixed (all translations and rotations held), pinned (translations held, rotations free), symmetry (planar: the normal displacement is held on the target faces), displacement (prescribed dofs, e.g. { uz: 0 }; 0 holds a dof). target points at the faces / edges / vertices of a PART of the analysis by points near them (facesNear etc., document units): the nearest topology is chosen when the mesh is built, so pick points well inside the intended face. Under-constrained models are reported by check_analysis once built.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

dofs.description: displacement only: prescribed degrees of freedom as an object with any of the keys ux, uy, uz (document length units), rx, ry, rz (radians); 0 holds the dof, absent = free; at least one required, e.g. { "uz": 0 }.

target.description: Where the constraint applies.

edgesNear.description: Points identifying edges: each resolves to the nearest edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended edge.

entityId.description: Id of the analysed 3D entity (it must be a part of the analysis: set_part_idealization).

facesNear.description: Points identifying faces: each resolves to the NEAREST face of the entity at meshing time.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended face.

intersectPlane.description: Optional: restrict the target to the curve where the faces meet this plane.

normal.description: Plane normal (need not be unit length).

pointsNear.description: Points identifying vertices / locations: each resolves to the nearest vertex or node.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended vertex or location.

name: add_fea_constraint

description: Add a mechanical load to an analysis, returning the load id in affected[0]. kind: force (vector on target faces / edges / points; "total" spreads it, "per_node" applies it at each node), pressure (magnitude normal to the target faces, positive = into the material) or gravity (acceleration vector, no target). Magnitudes are in the unit system of the analysis (see describe_analysis, case.unitSystem; N-mm-t-s: N, MPa and gravity 9810 mm/s^2). loadCase groups loads solved together; category limit | ultimate drives later margin factors. Moments are not built. The target is given as points near the topology (see add_fea_constraint).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

distribution.description: force only: "total" (default) spreads the vector over the target; "per_node" applies it at every target node.

loadCase.description: Load case name this load belongs to: 1-40 letters, digits or underscores (e.g. "LC1", "landing_2"). Default "LC1".

magnitude.description: pressure only: positive pushes INTO the material (compressive), negative pulls (in the case unitSystem: N-mm-t-s -> N, MPa, mm/s^2 (9.81 m/s^2 = 9810); N-m-kg-s -> N, Pa, m/s^2; lbf-in-slinch-s -> lbf, psi, in/s^2).

target.description: force / pressure: the faces (edges, points for force) the load acts on. Not for gravity.

edgesNear.description: Points identifying edges: each resolves to the nearest edge.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended edge.

entityId.description: Id of the analysed 3D entity (it must be a part of the analysis: set_part_idealization).

facesNear.description: Points identifying faces: each resolves to the NEAREST face of the entity at meshing time.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended face.

intersectPlane.description: Optional: restrict the target to the curve where the faces meet this plane.

normal.description: Plane normal (need not be unit length).

pointsNear.description: Points identifying vertices / locations: each resolves to the nearest vertex or node.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] in document units lying on (or very near) the intended vertex or location.

vector.description: force / gravity: direction and magnitude [x, y, z] (in the case unitSystem: N-mm-t-s -> N, MPa, mm/s^2 (9.81 m/s^2 = 9810); N-m-kg-s -> N, Pa, m/s^2; lbf-in-slinch-s -> lbf, psi, in/s^2). Not for pressure.

name: add_fea_load

description: Add an edge flange (a bend plus a flat leg) to a sheet-metal part on a straight outline edge picked by a world point `edge.near` (any point within one thickness of the edge). angle is the angle bent THROUGH in degrees (90 = right angle; a closed 45-degree angle is a 135-degree bend); direction up bends towards the flat's +normal face. length is measured from the bend to the free end along the flange: to the outside mold line (virtual sharp of the outer faces, default for drawings), the inside mold line, or the bend tangent line. position says where the picked edge sits: 'material_outside' = the edge is the bend tangent line (the bend grows outside the profile), 'material_inside' = the edge is the outside mold line (the flat is trimmed back by the outside setback), 'bend_outside' = the edge is the extreme of the outer bend surface. insideRadius defaults to the rule radius. widthStart / widthEnd inset the bend from the edge ends. All lengths are in the document length unit. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_BEND_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_SHARP_BEND_FORBIDDEN (R = 0), FTR_EDGE_NOT_STRAIGHT (no edge at edge.near), FTR_EDGE_OCCUPIED, FTR_FLANGE_TOO_SHORT. Next: add_relief, add_sheet_cutout, flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

angle.description: Bend angle in degrees: the angle bent THROUGH (0 = flat, 90 = right angle). 0 < angle <= 180; 180 only with lengthReference tangent.

autoRelief.description: Default true: when the rule defines a rectangular relief, cut it automatically at each end of the new bend that stops short of the edge end (width = widthRatio x thickness, depth = inside radius + thickness + depthExtra, all in the document length unit; the result's data.reliefs names the defaulted values). false = leave the bend ends unrelieved (check_sheet_metal then warns FTR_RELIEF_MISSING).

direction.description: Bend towards the flat's +normal face ('up', default) or the -normal face ('down').

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or within one thickness of the straight edge that receives the flange (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

insideRadius.description: Inside bend radius in the document length unit; default the rule radius; >= 0.

length.description: Flange length in the document length unit, measured as lengthReference says; must leave a flat leg > 0.

lengthReference.description: Where `length` ends at the bend: 'outside_mold_line', 'inside_mold_line' or 'tangent' (the bend tangent line).

position.description: Where the picked edge sits relative to the bend: 'material_outside', 'material_inside' or 'bend_outside'.

widthEnd.description: Inset of the flange from the edge end, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

widthStart.description: Inset of the flange from the edge start, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

name: add_flange

description: Add a flanged (lightening) hole to ONE flat of a sheet-metal part: a hole with a lip bent up or down around it, as on stiffened ribs. The flat is picked by the world point `face.near`; `center` is the hole axis point [x, y, z] (projected onto the flat). holeDiameter is the bore diameter of the lip where the bend starts; flangeHeight is the rise of the free end of the lip above the flat face on the lip side; flangeAngle is the angle bent through in degrees (0 < angle <= 90; 90 = cylindrical lip); lipRadius is the inside radius of the bend between flat and lip. The physical hole in the flat has radius holeDiameter/2 + thickness + lipRadius (data.cutRadius). In the flat pattern the hole is DEVELOPED to a smaller circle (data.flatCutDiameter) flagged approximate and unverified (stretch flange): do not cut it without a trial. All lengths are in the document length unit. The hole and its lip must lie wholly inside the flat, clear of its edges, bends, cutouts and beads. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FORM_INVALID, FTR_CUTOUT_INVALID. Next: flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

center.description: World point [x, y, z] of the hole axis (document length unit); projected onto the flat plane.

direction.description: Lip towards the flat's +normal face ('up', default) or the -normal face ('down').

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or near the flat that gets the hole (document length unit).

flangeAngle.description: Angle the lip is bent through, in degrees: 0 < angle <= 90 (90 = cylindrical lip).

flangeHeight.description: Rise of the lip free end above the flat face on the lip side, in the document length unit; must exceed lipRadius*(1-cos(angle)).

holeDiameter.description: Bore diameter of the lip where the bend starts, in the document length unit; > 0.

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

lipRadius.description: Inside (concave) radius of the bend between flat and lip, in the document length unit; > 0.

name: add_flanged_hole

description: Add concrete pad footings: one at a plan location, or (underColumns: true) one under every steel and concrete column foot of the level (underColumns wins over location). With underColumns, feet that already carry a footing on the level (within 10 mm) are skipped and the command is refused when none is left; an explicit location that already carries a footing on the level (within 10 mm) is refused. Top of footing at level + topOffset (default −300 mm); default 1500 × 1500 × 600 mm.

length.description: Size along Y, in document units. Default = width.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

thickness.description: Depth of the pad, in document units. Default 600 mm.

topOffset.description: Top of footing relative to the level, in document units. Default −300 mm.

underColumns.description: Place one under each steel or concrete column foot of the level (ignores location).

width.description: Size along X, in document units. Default 1500 mm.

name: add_footing

description: Couple two joints rigidly, like meshing gears, a belt or a chain: speed(driven) = ratio × speed(driver), enforced by the physics engine, so each side feels the other's inertia and load. ratio = -teeth(driver)/teeth(driven) for an external spur mesh (opposite rotation), +teeth(driver)/teeth(driven) for a belt or an internal ring gear. Planetary with fixed ring, sun → carrier: ratio = sunTeeth / (sunTeeth + ringTeeth). Planets relative to the carrier: -ringTeeth / planetTeeth (driver = carrier joint). Returns the coupling id in affected[0].

driven.description: Joint id that follows (e.g. the propeller joint).

driver.description: Joint id whose speed drives the other (e.g. the crankshaft joint).

id.description: Optional explicit coupling id.

ratio.description: speed(driven) / speed(driver); negative reverses the direction.

name: add_gear_coupling

description: Frame beams along the structural grid (add_grid_line): along every listed grid line, one beam per bay between consecutive intersections with the other lines (so it frames column to column when add_grid_columns was run first). The beam top sits at the level FFL + topOffset (reference "ffl", default) or at the level top (FFL + level height) + topOffset (reference "levelTop"). Bays that already hold a beam with the same end points and a top of steel within 100 mm are skipped (any section). Mark SB, role beam.

axes.description: Grid line labels to frame along (e.g. ["A","B"]). Default: every grid line.

endJoint.description: Joint at each beam end: "pinned" (default) or "rigid".

levelId.description: Level id: the beams sit at its finished floor level. Default: the active level.

reference.description: Datum of topOffset: "levelTop" = level elevation + level height (underside of the next floor), "ffl" = level finished floor elevation. The same reference and topOffset put add_beam and add_grid_beams at the same absolute elevation. Default differs by domain and is kept so existing documents replay unchanged: add_beam "levelTop" (concrete beam under the next slab), add_grid_beams "ffl" (steel framing referenced to finished floor). Pass reference explicitly to be unambiguous; the summary states the resolved elevation.

startJoint.description: Joint at each beam start: "pinned" (default) or "rigid" (moment connection).

topOffset.description: Top of steel relative to the level FFL, in DOCUMENT UNITS (not necessarily mm). Default 0 (top of steel at FFL); negative puts it below the FFL, e.g. minus the grating thickness.

name: add_grid_beams

description: Add vertical bracing in one bay of one grid line for one storey: the bay lies in the plane of grid line axis between the crossing lines from and to. pattern "x" gives two crossing diagonals, "diagonal" one from bottom at from to top at to. Bottom nodes sit at the base level FFL + bottomOffset, top nodes at the next storey FFL (base elevation + level height) + topOffset. Mark BR, role brace.

axis.description: Label of the grid line the bracing lies in, e.g. "A".

bottomOffset.description: Bottom node height relative to the base level FFL, in DOCUMENT UNITS (not necessarily mm). Default 0 (at the FFL).

from.description: Label of the grid line crossing axis that bounds the bay at one side, e.g. "1".

levelId.description: Storey base level id: bracing starts at its FFL and rises one level height. Default: the active level.

pattern.description: "x" (default): two crossing diagonals; "diagonal": one, from bottom at from to top at to.

to.description: Label of the grid line crossing axis that bounds the bay at the other side, e.g. "2".

topOffset.description: Top node height relative to the NEXT storey FFL (base elevation + level height), in DOCUMENT UNITS (not necessarily mm). Default 0 (at the next FFL); negative puts the node under the floor beams.

name: add_grid_bracing

description: Place one vertical steel column at every intersection of the structural grid (add_grid_line): the way to start framing a building. The column runs from the base level FFL up to topLevelId (a continuous column through intermediate floors) or, by default, to the top of the base level. Restrict with axes (both crossing lines must be listed) and exclude. Intersections that already hold a column on that level, or a continuous column from a lower level passing through it, are skipped. Mark SC, role column; follow with add_grid_beams / add_grid_bracing.

axes.description: Grid line labels (e.g. ["A","B","1","2"]); an intersection is used only when BOTH its lines are listed. Default: all grid lines.

baseFixity.description: "pinned" (default) or "fixed": the column foot restrains rotation in check_steel_members.

exclude.description: Intersections to skip, written "A/1" (the order of the two labels does not matter).

levelId.description: Base level id: columns start at its finished floor level. Default: the active level.

roll.description: Section rotation about the vertical axis, radians. Default 0.

topLevelId.description: Level id whose FFL is the column top; must be above the base level. Default: base level elevation + base level height.

name: add_grid_columns

description: Add one structural grid axis from start to end (plan [x, y]) with a labelled bubble at each end, on layer S-GRID. Label defaults to the next free number. Refused if an axis with the same end points exists.

label.description: Bubble label, e.g. "A" or "3". Must be unique.

name: add_grid_line

description: Lay out a rectangular structural grid. Numbered axes 1, 2, 3… run parallel to Y and are spaced along X by xSpacings; lettered axes A, B, C… (I and O skipped) run parallel to X, spaced along Y by ySpacings. E.g. xSpacings [6000, 6000] gives axes 1–3 six metres apart. Refused when every axis of the new grid already exists; otherwise labels continue after the existing ones.

extension.description: How far axes overrun the outer grid lines (document units). Default 1500 mm.

origin.description: Intersection of axis 1 and axis A [x, y]. Default [0, 0].

xSpacings.description: Bay widths along X between consecutive numbered axes (each > 0, at most 100).

ySpacings.description: Bay widths along Y between consecutive lettered axes (each > 0, at most 100).

name: add_grid_system

description: Create a helical compression spring as one sweep solid (round wire swept along a smooth helix spline). The spring axis runs from position along axis (default +Z); the base plane center is at position and the spring extends to position + axis * free length, wire thickness included. Wire size: give wireRadius or wireDiameter. coilRadius is the MEAN coil radius (axis to wire centerline) and must exceed wireRadius. Give at least two of pitch (centerline advance per turn, >= wire diameter), turns (number of coils, may be fractional, <= 200) and length (free length = overall extent along the axis incl. wire). Pitch and turns win if all three are given. closedEnds=true flattens the first and last turn (pitch = wire diameter) like ground/closed spring ends; the middle turns get the pitch needed to keep the overall length (requires turns > 2). The result is a sweep entity, so booleans, measuring, rendering and STEP/STL export work like any solid. Returns the entity id and data {freeLength, turns, pitch, wireDiameter, outerDiameter}.

axis.description: Direction [dx, dy, dz] (non-zero, normalized) the spring extends along from position. Defaults to [0, 0, 1].

closedEnds.description: Flatten the first and last turn to wire-diameter pitch. Default false. Needs turns > 2.

coilRadius.description: Mean coil radius (axis to wire centerline) in document units; must be > wire radius.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#8a8f98".

length.description: Free length along the axis incl. wire thickness, document units.

pitch.description: Centerline advance along the axis per full turn, document units; >= wire diameter.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Center of the spring base plane (start of the spring). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

turns.description: Number of coils (may be fractional), 0 < turns <= 200.

wireDiameter.description: Wire diameter in document units (> 0). Used when wireRadius is absent.

wireRadius.description: Wire radius in document units (> 0). Alternative: wireDiameter.

name: add_helix_spring

description: Add a 180-degree hem (a flat folded back over itself along a straight edge) to a sheet-metal part: a 180-degree bend followed by a straight return leg. The edge is picked by the world point `edge.near` (within one thickness of the edge) and is the bend tangent line. hemType 'closed' = no gap (inside radius 0, the return leg lies against the flat; allowed even when the rule forbids sharp bends); 'open' = a gap between the flat and the return leg (inside radius = gap/2, gap required). length is the straight return leg after the bend, from the bend tangent line to the free edge. All lengths are in the document length unit. The developed length of the hem (flat_pattern data.hems[]) is pi*(gap/2 + K*T) + length with the rule K at that radius: the neutral-surface model extended to 180 degrees, flagged UNVERIFIED (not checked against a published hem table). The teardrop hem is not supported. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_FLANGE_TOO_SHORT, FTR_EDGE_NOT_STRAIGHT, FTR_EDGE_OCCUPIED. Next: flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

direction.description: Fold towards the flat's +normal face ('up', default) or the -normal face ('down').

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or within one thickness of the straight edge that gets the hem (document length unit).

gap.description: Clear gap between the flat and the return leg in the document length unit; required and > 0 for an open hem, omitted for a closed hem. Inside radius = gap/2.

hemType.description: 'closed' = zero gap (inside radius 0); 'open' = gap between flat and return leg.

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

length.description: Straight return leg length after the bend in the document length unit; > 0.

widthEnd.description: Inset of the hem from the edge end, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

widthStart.description: Inset of the hem from the edge start, in the document length unit (>= 0, default 0).

name: add_hem

description: Cut holes into a planar face of a 3D solid: simple, counterbore, countersink or counterdrill (countersink cone, then counterbore, then bore); through the whole part (through_all), through the first wall only (up_to_next), up to the plane of a parallel face below (up_to_face, extent.face.near) or blind with a drill point (default 118 degrees, reported as defaulted; drillPointAngle 0 = flat bottom). The face is picked by a world point on it (face.near); the holes go INTO the material, along the opposite of the face outward normal. All lengths are in the document length unit, all angles in degrees. points: [u, v] in the face frame (origin = the world origin projected on the face plane, u = world X (or Y) projected on it, v = normal x u), or pointsFrame "world_xy" ([x, y] world, the point is moved along Z onto the face), or "world" ([x, y, z] projected onto the face). All positions are validated first: if one is bad nothing is cut. hole.thread is a cosmetic attribute (geometry unchanged) unless thread.modelled is true (a real helical groove). hole.fastener takes the clearance diameter from the document fastener catalogue. Consumes target and creates one mesh entity (exact B-rep with an exact kernel). Refusals carry error.code: FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_PLANAR, FTR_HOLE_POINT_OUTSIDE_FACE, FTR_HOLE_DIAMETERS_INCONSISTENT, FTR_CSK_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_BLIND_DEPTH_INVALID, FTR_DRILL_POINT_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_THREAD_DESIGNATION_INVALID, FTR_FASTENER_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE, FTR_UP_TO_TARGET_INVALID, FTR_FEATURE_BUILD_FAILED. Next: check_machining, hole_table, recognize_features.

depth.description: Blind only: cylindrical depth from the face, in document length units (drill point excluded). Must be inside the stock.

drillPointAngle.description: Blind only: drill point included angle in degrees in (0, 180); 0 = flat bottom. Omitted = 118 (named as defaulted).

face.description: up_to_face only: the planar target face the hole stops at, picked by a world point.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on the planar target face, in document length units.

kind.description: "through_all" cuts through the whole part along the axis; "blind" stops at depth; "up_to_next" cuts through the first wall only (until the axis leaves the material, measured per hole: refined on the exact faces of the kernel when it has them (OpenCascade), else on the display mesh, which is only accurate to the tessellation on curved exit walls; the summary says which); "up_to_face" stops at the plane of the planar face picked by face.near, which must be parallel to the hole face and below it.

face.description: The planar face to drill into, picked by a world point.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on (or within 0.1% of the part size of) the planar face, in document length units.

hole.description: Hole definition: kind, diameters, optional thread (cosmetic, or a modelled helical groove) and fastener reference.

cboreDepth.description: Counterbore (or counterdrill) depth from the face, in document length units; a counterdrill needs it below the cone.

cboreDiameter.description: Counterbore (or counterdrill) diameter, in document length units; must exceed diameter.

cskAngle.description: Countersink included angle in degrees, in (0, 180), e.g. 82, 90, 100.

cskDepth.description: Countersink cone depth from the face, in document length units. Alternative to cskDiameter (D = d + 2*depth*tan(angle/2)).

cskDiameter.description: Countersink diameter at the face, in document length units; must exceed diameter (counterdrill: must exceed cboreDiameter). Alternative to cskDepth.

diameter.description: Bore diameter, in document length units. Required unless fastener gives it from the catalogue.

fastener.description: Standard fastener this hole is for: its clearance hole diameter comes from the document fastener catalogue.

fit.description: Optional fit label recorded with the hole (no geometric effect).

partNumber.description: Part number; its dash token selects the catalogue size, whose hole diameter is used.

kind.description: "simple" (plain bore), "counterbore" (needs cboreDiameter, cboreDepth), "countersink" (needs cskAngle and cskDiameter or cskDepth) or "counterdrill" (a countersink cone from the face down to the counterbore, then the counterbore, then the bore: needs cboreDiameter, cboreDepth, cskAngle and cskDiameter or cskDepth; cskDiameter > cboreDiameter > diameter).

thread.description: Thread attribute of the hole: cosmetic by default, a real helical groove when modelled is true.

depth.description: Threaded depth, in document length units. Omit for the full hole depth.

designation.description: Thread designation, e.g. "MJ6x1-4H5H", ".1900-32 UNJF-3B", "M6x1-6H", "1/4-20 UNC-2B". Cosmetic unless modelled is true.

family.description: Thread family (UNJ, MJ, UN, M, other). Omit to infer it from the designation.
