modelled.description: true cuts a real helical thread groove (basic 60 degree internal ISO 68-1 profile; M / MJ / UN / UNJ designations with an explicit pitch, e.g. "M6x1"; MJ / UNJ root radius not applied, unverified) into the hole: the bore diameter must be about the minor diameter (D - 1.0825 P) and below the major diameter; needs a geometry kernel; changes the geometry and the shape recipe key. Omit or false = cosmetic, no geometry.

points.description: Hole centres, in document length units: [u, v] (pointsFrame face), [x, y] (world_xy) or [x, y, z] (world). At least one.

pointsFrame.description: Coordinates of points: "face" (default), "world_xy" or "world". See the command description.

target.description: Id of the 3D solid to drill (a primitive or a kernel result).

name: add_hole

description: Place a raster image (a scanned drawing, a photo of a sketch) on a 2D work plane as a semi-transparent underlay to trace over. The lower-left corner of the image sits at `position`; size it with `width` (document units) OR `pixelSize` (document units per pixel, e.g. 1.5 for 1.5 mm/px); with neither, 1 unit per pixel. Then use calibrate_underlay (two pixel points + their real distance) to fix the scale, origin and orientation, and image_to_world to convert pixel coordinates read off the picture into model coordinates for draw_polyline / extrude_profile / revolve_profile. Accepts PNG or JPEG base64 data URLs up to 8000000 characters.

dataUrl.description: The image as a base64 data URL: "data:image/png;base64,…" or "data:image/jpeg;base64,…".

locked.description: true: the viewport never picks/selects it while tracing. Defaults to false.

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

opacity.description: Opacity in [0, 1] (0 = invisible, 1 = opaque). Defaults to 0.5.

pixelSize.description: Document units per image pixel (> 0), e.g. 1.5 for a 1.5 mm/px scan. Excludes width.

position.description: World position [x, y, z] of the image lower-left corner (work-plane origin). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X) of the work plane. Defaults to [0, 0, 0].

width.description: Placed image width in document units (> 0); height follows the aspect ratio.

name: add_image_underlay

description: Create an internal (ring) involute gear: a cylindrical rim whose bore carries inward-pointing teeth, as ONE closed mesh solid built without booleans. Same tooth convention as add_spur_gear (addendum 1·module, dedendum 1.25·module), tooth spaces widened by 0.05·module backlash so an external gear of the same module and pressure angle meshes without interference. The ring is centred on its axis (+Z, z from 0 to faceWidth) at `position`; tooth pitch diameter = module * teeth. Pair with add_spur_gear: centre distance = module * (ringTeeth - pinionTeeth) / 2. For a complete sun/planet/ring set use add_planetary_gearset (it phases the teeth for you). The result is a world-space mesh entity (position/rotation are baked in).

color.description: Hex color. Default "#8892a0".

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

outerRadius.description: Radius of the cylindrical rim (outside of the ring). Must be >= pitchRadius + 2.25 * module so that material remains behind the tooth spaces.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the ring on its axis (z = bottom face). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Pressure angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Default 0.3491 (20°).

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

teeth.description: Number of internal teeth, integer >= 12 and <= 1000. Typical ring gears have 40-120.

name: add_internal_gear

description: Add a joggle (two reverse bends of angle phi that offset the rest of a flat by `offset`) across the full width of one flat of a sheet-metal part. The flat is picked by the world point `face.near`; `line` is the start tangent line of the first bend as two [x, y] points in the flat's own plane coordinates (for the base flat these are the profile coordinates); the line is extended to the flat's outline. The piece on the RIGHT of line[0] -> line[1] keeps the flat (for a flat that is attached through a bend the side attached to the bend is kept automatically); an inclined flat of length s and the offset piece are inserted on the LEFT. offset (the offset between the two flat faces), angle (degrees, 0 < angle <= 90) and insideRadius are in document length unit / degrees. Inclined straight s = (offset - 2*(R+T/2)*(1-cos(angle)))/sin(angle) must be > 0, else FTR_JOGGLE_OFFSET_TOO_SMALL (increase the offset to more than 2*(R+T/2)*(1-cos(angle)), or reduce R or angle). Other refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_BEND_ANGLE_OUT_OF_RANGE, FTR_SHARP_BEND_FORBIDDEN, FTR_JOGGLE_LINE_INVALID. flat_pattern then reports the joggle allowance and run.

angle.description: Joggle bend angle phi in degrees; 0 < angle <= 90.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or near the flat to joggle (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

insideRadius.description: Inside bend radius of both bends in the document length unit; default the rule radius; >= 0.

line.description: Start tangent line of the first joggle bend, as two [x, y] points in the picked flat's plane coordinates (document length unit).

items.description: Start of the line [x, y] in the flat plane coordinates (document length unit).

offset.description: Offset between the two flat faces in the document length unit; > 0.

side.description: Direction of the offset: 'up' moves the offset piece towards the flat's +normal side, 'down' towards -normal.

name: add_joggle

description: Add a kinematic joint between two InstanceEntity frames to model a mechanism. A "revolute" joint allows rotation of instance b around the given axis through instance a's origin. A "prismatic" joint allows translation of instance b along the given axis from instance a's origin. "a" and "b" are MateRef objects: { instanceId: "<id>", frame?: "origin"|"axis-x"|"axis-y"|"axis-z" }. "axis" is the rotation/slide axis: use "x", "y", or "z" for world axes, or a [x,y,z] unit vector. Initial joint value (angle / displacement) defaults to 0. Use set_joint_value to drive the joint. Use evaluate_motion or bake_motion to apply motion to instances. Returns the new joint id in affected[0].

a.description: First instance frame reference (the fixed/anchor frame). { instanceId: "<id>", frame?: "origin"|"axis-x"|"axis-y"|"axis-z" }. instanceId must be an existing InstanceEntity. frame defaults to "origin".

frame.description: Frame selector: origin (default), axis-x, axis-y, or axis-z.

axis.description: Rotation or slide axis. Use "x", "y", or "z" for world-aligned axes, or pass a [x,y,z] unit vector array for an arbitrary direction.

b.description: Second instance frame reference (the moving frame). { instanceId: "<id>", frame?: "origin"|"axis-x"|"axis-y"|"axis-z" }. instanceId must be an existing InstanceEntity. frame defaults to "origin".

frame.description: Frame selector: origin (default), axis-x, axis-y, or axis-z.

id.description: Optional explicit joint id. When omitted a unique id is generated. If the id already exists in doc.joints the command is a no-op.

kind.description: Joint type. "revolute": rotation about an axis (like a hinge or pin). "prismatic": linear translation along an axis (like a slider or piston).

name: add_joint

description: Create a round shaft along +Z (z from 0 to length) with a rectangular keyway (pocket) on its +X side, built as one closed mesh solid without booleans. Keyway width b, groove depth t1 (from the shaft surface to the groove floor) and the optional key height h default to the DIN 6885 form A values for the shaft diameter (e.g. d=40 -> b=12, t1=5, h=8). The pocket spans keyLength starting keyOffset above the bottom end (defaults: keyLength = 60% of length, centred); keyOffset 0 or reaching the top gives an open-ended keyway. includeKey=true also creates the matching parallel key as a separate mesh solid seated in the groove (affected = [shaft, key]). Result is world-space mesh entities.

color.description: Shaft hex color. Default "#9aa3ad".

includeKey.description: Also create the parallel key part. Default false.

keyDepth.description: Groove depth t1 measured from the shaft surface. Default from DIN 6885.

keyHeight.description: Key height h (only used when includeKey is true). Default from DIN 6885.

keyLength.description: Keyway length along the shaft, > 0 and <= length. Default 60% of length.

keyOffset.description: Distance from the shaft bottom end (z = 0) to the keyway start, >= 0. Default centred.

keyWidth.description: Keyway width b. Default from DIN 6885 for the diameter.

name.description: Optional display name for the shaft.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the shaft bottom face. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_keyed_shaft

description: Create a new layer with the given name and append it to the layer order. Returns the new layer id in affected. The layer starts visible and unlocked.

color.description: Optional hex color string #rrggbb for the layer, e.g. "#ff0000"; any other format is rejected. Used by the UI to tint layer contents. Omit to leave unset.

name.description: Human-readable name for the new layer, e.g. "Walls". Must be non-empty.

name: add_layer

description: Add a building level (storey). Elevation is the finished-floor height; height is floor-to-floor. Defaults: elevation = top of the highest existing level (or 0), height = 3000 mm. Building elements (walls, slabs, columns…) are placed relative to their level.

elevation.description: Finished-floor elevation in document units. Default: stacks on the top level.

height.description: Floor-to-floor height in document units (> 0). Default 3000 mm.

makeActive.description: Make it the active level for new elements. Default true.

name: add_level

description: Add a drainage manhole / inspection chamber / outfall at a plan position. Give `invertElevation` and either `rimElevation` or a `surfaceId` (rim = ground level there). Optional catchment (area in ha, runoff coefficient), point inflow and `entryTimeMin` (inlet time, default 5 min) feed the network check. Connect manholes with add_pipe.

catchmentAreaHa.description: Contributing catchment area in hectares (> 0) for the rational method.

diameter.description: Chamber internal diameter in document units (> 0). Default 1200 mm.

entryTimeMin.description: Inlet (entry) time in minutes (> 0) of this manhole's catchment for the time of concentration. Default 5.

inflowLps.description: Additional point inflow in litres per second (>= 0).

invertElevation.description: Invert (lowest internal) elevation of the chamber.

location.description: Plan position [x, y] of the chamber centre, document units.

rimElevation.description: Rim (cover level) elevation; must be above the invert. Overrides `surfaceId`.

runoffCoefficient.description: Runoff coefficient C, 0 to 1. Default 0.9 when a catchment area is given.

surfaceId.description: Surface id; when `rimElevation` is omitted the rim is the ground level there.

name: add_manhole

description: Attach a constitutive or durability law to a material (create_material first): linear elasticity (isotropic, orthotropic, transversely isotropic, anisotropic), J2 plasticity with isotropic and kinematic hardening, Ramberg-Osgood, hyperelasticity (Neo-Hooke, Mooney-Rivlin, polynomial, Yeoh, Ogden, Arruda-Boyce), Prony viscoelasticity, Norton / Garofalo creep, Johnson-Cook / Cowper-Symonds rate laws, and the fatigue / crack-growth variants. Parameters carry units; conventions are stated, never guessed (linear hardening needs modulusKind plastic or tangent, curves need their measure, Ogden needs its convention, Ramberg-Osgood its form); llull stores the canonical form and records the conversion. Elastic stiffness must be positive definite and a hyperelastic law Drucker-stable inside its declared stretch validity. The parameter hash is recomputed. Next: define_constitutive_set, then material_point_response and check_material_models.

basis.description: A | B | S, typical, supplier_unstated, company, unspecified (typical / unstated / unspecified ⇒ unverified).

fit.description: Fit record exactly as returned by fit_material_model (never hand-written).

id.description: Model id, unique on the material, e.g. "elastic", "plastic.iso", "treloar.yeoh".

material.description: Material id: the name given to create_material.

model.description: The law, by kind. ELASTIC: elastic_isotropic {E, nu}; elastic_orthotropic {E1,E2,E3,nu12,nu13,nu23,G12,G13,G23}; elastic_transversely_isotropic {isotropyPlane '12'|'23', Ep, Et, nuP, nuPT, Gt}; elastic_anisotropic {stiffness: 21 numbers, upper triangle row-wise in Voigt order 11 22 33 12 13 23 (engineering shear), unit}. PLASTIC: j2_plasticity {isotropic: perfect {yieldStress} | linear {yieldStress, modulus, modulusKind plastic|tangent REQUIRED} | multilinear {stressUnit, curves [{temperature?, points [[stress, plasticStrain]…]}], inputMeasure {stress true|engineering, strain plastic|total, strainKind true|engineering, youngModulus? for total} REQUIRED} | voce {yieldStress, Q, b} | johnson_cook {A, B, n, m, meltTemperature, transitionTemperature}; kinematic: none | linear {C} | chaboche {backstresses [{C, gamma}…]}}; ramberg_osgood {form 'calculix' {E, nu, sigma0, alpha, n} | 'engineering' {E, nu, sigma02, n} REQUIRED}. HYPERELASTIC (stress parameters {value, unit}, D in 1/stress, D = 0 incompressible): hyper_neo_hooke {C10, D1}; hyper_mooney_rivlin {C10, C01, D1}; hyper_polynomial {order, C {C10…}, D[], stressUnit}; hyper_reduced_polynomial {order, Ci0[], D[], stressUnit}; hyper_yeoh {C10, C20, C30, D[3], compliance}; hyper_ogden {convention 'calculix'|'ogden1972' REQUIRED, terms [{mu, alpha}] (1-3), D[], stressUnit}; hyper_arruda_boyce {mu, lambdaM, D}. TIME: visco_prony {shear [{g, tau}], bulk?, shift? wlf|arrhenius}; creep_norton {A, n, m, stressUnit, timeUnit, hardening}; creep_garofalo {A, alpha, n, activationEnergy}; rate_johnson_cook {C, referenceRate}; rate_cowper_symonds {D, q}. DURABILITY (stored and validated structurally, never in a set): sn_basquin, sn_power_law, sn_table, sn_equivalent_stress, en_coffin_manson, cyclic_ramberg_osgood, haigh_table, da_dn_paris, da_dn_walker, da_dn_forman, da_dn_nasgro, da_dn_table, fracture_toughness. A stress-like parameter is {value, unit} or {propertyModelId} (a define_property_model model of the same material, e.g. E(T)).

preferred.description: Mark as THE model of its kind on the material (one per kind).

replace.description: Replace an existing model with the same id (default false: refused with MATL_MODEL_EXISTS).

source.description: Provenance of the parameters (required).

locator.description: Table / page / figure in the source.

sourceId.description: Registered source id, when one exists.

validity.description: Ranges the law is valid in (T, equivalentPlasticStrain, strainRate, time, stretch): REQUIRED for exports, advised for every constitutive law.

data.description: [min, max] of the data the parameters were derived from.

equation.description: [min, max] the source allows (⊇ data; default = data).

unit.description: Unit of the bounds, e.g. 'K', '1/s', '1'.

variable.description: State variable the range applies to: T, strainRate, time, equivalentPlasticStrain, stretch …

name: add_material_model

description: Detail the portal frame moment connections: a bolted end plate at every rafter-to-column joint (eaves, with a haunch under the rafter) and a pair of end plates at every rafter-to-rafter joint (apex), for the given rafters or every rafter of the level. Sized from the rafter section (plate 20/25 mm, M20 bolts, haunch = 1/5 of the rafter plan length). Follows the rafter; plate, haunch and bolt quantities feed the takeoff and the connection schedule.

apexHaunchLength.description: Apex haunch length along each of the two rafters meeting at the ridge, in document units. Default none.

boltDiameter.description: Bolt diameter, in document units. Default 20 mm (M20).

haunchLength.description: Eaves haunch length along the rafter. Default 1/5 of its plan length.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level.

plateThickness.description: End plate thickness, in document units. Default 20 / 25 mm.

rafterIds.description: Rafter member ids. Default: every rafter of the level.

name: add_moment_connections

description: Drive a joint for simulate_motion. kind "torque_curve" = an engine or electric motor: torque (N·m) vs shaft speed (rpm) at full throttle, e.g. curve [[0, 300], [2000, 420], [2800, 400], [3200, 0]], times `throttle` (0..1). A single constant torque: `torque: 50` (same as a one-point curve). The speed then rises until the load (propeller, friction, damping) absorbs the torque — the physically settled operating point. kind "speed" = a governed drive that holds `rpm` using at most `maxTorque` N·m (a test rig / constant-speed prop governor). Torque acts in the joint's positive direction (right-hand rule about the joint axis). Returns the motor id in affected[0].

curve.description: torque_curve: [[rpm, torque N·m], …] with increasing rpm; linear between points, held flat outside them.

id.description: Optional explicit motor id.

joint.description: Joint id to drive (e.g. the crankshaft joint).

kind.description: "torque_curve" = engine (torque vs rpm); "speed" = holds a set rpm.

rpm.description: speed: target shaft speed in rpm.

throttle.description: torque_curve: fraction of the curve torque, 0..1. Default 1.

torque.description: torque_curve shortcut: one constant torque in N·m (instead of curve).

name: add_motor

description: Add a planar cladding, roofing or sandwich panel through 3D corners [[x, y, z], …] (z above the level). The panel thickness grows along the plane normal (right-hand rule on the corner order). Use for pitched roofs, façades and gables.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

role.description: Roofing or wall cladding. Default wall.

thickness.description: Panel thickness, in document units. Default 80 mm.

name: add_panel

description: Add a gravity pipe from the upstream manhole `fromId` to the downstream manhole `toId` (flow direction). Inverts default to the manhole inverts; diameter 300 mm, PVC, n 0.013. Refuses self-loops, duplicates and loops in the network; warns on adverse (uphill) slope. Then run check_drainage_network or size_drainage_pipes.

diameter.description: Pipe internal diameter in document units (> 0). Default 300 mm.

invertFrom.description: Invert elevation at the upstream end. Default: upstream manhole invert.

invertTo.description: Invert elevation at the downstream end. Default: downstream manhole invert.

name: add_pipe

description: Route a pipe through 3D points [[x, y, z], …] (z above the level) with a service / fluid name (compressed air, cooling water, steam, gas…) and line-list data: line number, nominal size DN and from / to ends. Give `dn` (e.g. 100) and the outside diameter is taken from the EN 10220 / ASME B36.10 table (15…400); `diameter` overrides it. Bends are placed at every interior point. Pipe lengths feed the takeoff; the pipe schedule (building_schedule kind "pipe") is the line list; clashes are reported by check_clashes. Support it with add_pipe_support and verify the spacing with check_pipe_supports. Refused if a pipe of the same diameter already follows the same route (either direction) on the level.

asBuilt.description: Set by commit_asbuilt_extraction: marks the run as scan-derived (as-built). Do not set it by hand.

unverified.description: Whether the scan-derived geometry is unverified.

diameter.description: Outside diameter in document units. Default: from `dn` when given, else 114.3 mm (DN100).

dn.description: Nominal size DN as an integer, e.g. 100. Tabulated: 15, 20, 25, 32, 40, 50, 65, 80, 100, 125, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 400. Sets the outside diameter when `diameter` is omitted (an untabulated DN then needs an explicit `diameter`). Printed "DN100" in the line list.

from.description: Line origin: equipment tag (e.g. "EQ1") or battery-limit / tie-in id (e.g. "BL-1").

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

line.description: Line number for the line list, e.g. "L-101".

points.description: Pipe centreline [[x, y, z], …], 2 to 1000 points.

to.description: Line destination: equipment tag or battery-limit / tie-in id.

name: add_pipe_run

description: Place supports on an existing pipe (add_pipe_run) so its weight reaches the steel (check_steel_members) and its spans can be verified (check_pipe_supports). Select the pipe with `pipeId` (element id) or `line` (line number, every pipe carrying it) and give EITHER `at` (list of absolute [x, y, z] points, each snapped to the nearest point of the pipe centreline within `snapDistance`) OR `spacing` (auto-placed along the pipe at no more than that spacing, plus one support min(300 mm, spacing/4) from each free end and one near each bend; ends inside equipment or on another pipe are carried and get none; never on risers). `type`: "shoe" (pipe rests on steel below), "hanger" (rod from steel above), "guide" (shoe with side stops), "anchor" (shoe fixed to the steel); all four carry the pipe weight on a horizontal run. ON A RISER (a segment steeper than 44° from horizontal, |dz|/length > 0.7; give an `at` point on it, `spacing` never places there) only guide / shoe / anchor are allowed and they are clamps with a horizontal bracket to steel BESIDE the pipe: a guide restrains it laterally (checked by check_pipe_supports riser rule: lateral restraint spacing and a support carrying the riser weight), a shoe or anchor also carries the riser weight (an anchor is a guide and a weight support). The steel it bears on is `memberId` or the nearest steel member in the right direction (below for shoe / guide / anchor, above for a hanger) within `maxReach` vertically and within half its width + `planTolerance` in plan (riser: a column, or a horizontal member whose section reaches the clamp elevation ± planTolerance, with its face within `maxReach` horizontally of the pipe surface). A position with no steel in reach is still created but UNATTACHED (memberId null): it carries nothing and the summary warns. Supports follow their pipe (moved, copied, deleted with it) and follow edits of their steel: deleting or moving a member or moving the pipe re-attaches them to the nearest steel in reach, or leaves them unattached (the edit command's summary lists which). Marks PS1, PS2… data.supports lists { id, mark, pipeId, type, position (level-relative), memberId, rodLength, standoff (riser bracket length) }.

at.description: Absolute support points [[x, y, z], …] in document units (z = elevation, not level-relative), on or near the pipe centreline: each is snapped to the nearest point of the pipe. At most 500 points per call. Give this OR `spacing`.

line.description: Line number of the pipe(s), e.g. "L-101" (the `line` given to add_pipe_run). Or use `pipeId`.

maxReach.description: Largest vertical gap between the pipe and its steel, document units, > 0: pedestal height for shoe / guide / anchor (default 500 mm), rod length for a hanger (default 3000 mm); on a riser the largest horizontal gap from the pipe surface to the member face (default 500 mm).

memberId.description: Element id of the steel member (add_steel_member data.elementId) every support bears on. Default: the nearest member in reach for each support.

pipeId.description: Element id of the pipe, e.g. "pipe-3" (from add_pipe_run data.elementId). Or use `line`.

planTolerance.description: Plan distance allowed beyond half the member width between the support and the member axis, document units, ≥ 0. Default 100 mm.

snapDistance.description: Largest distance from an `at` point to the pipe centreline, document units, > 0. Default 500 mm.

snapToSteel.description: With `spacing`: put the supports where the pipe crosses steel (one at each beam / member the centreline passes over or under, bearing on it) and treat `spacing` as the MAXIMUM allowed span between supports: no support is added away from steel, and the summary (data.spanWarnings) warns about every span longer than `spacing` or than the pipe-size table span, and every free end overhanging by more than half the spacing. A member running alongside the pipe is not a crossing. Pipes crossing no steel fall back to plain spacing placement (unattached supports, warned). Default true; false = plain spacing placement only. Ignored with `at`.

spacing.description: Maximum distance between supports along the pipe, document units, > 0: supports are auto-placed along the pipe (also near free ends and bends); refused when pipe length / spacing exceeds 500 supports on a run. Give this OR `at`. Existing supports are kept and counted. Where the pipe crosses steel the supports go on that steel and this is the maximum allowed span (see `snapToSteel`, default on).

type.description: "shoe" (rests on steel below, default), "hanger" (rod from steel above), "guide" (shoe with side stops; on a riser a lateral guide clamp) or "anchor" (fixed shoe; on a riser a clamp that guides and carries the weight).

name: add_pipe_support

description: Create a complete planetary (epicyclic) gear stage: one sun gear, planetCount planet gears and an internal ring gear, all sharing one module and pressure angle, with tooth phasing computed so that every planet meshes with the sun and the ring without interference. ringTeeth = sunTeeth + 2*planetTeeth. Assembly condition: (sunTeeth + ringTeeth) must be divisible by planetCount (e.g. sun 12, planet 18 -> ring 48, sum 60: planetCount 1-6, 10 or 12 work); otherwise the command is rejected and the summary lists the valid planetCounts. Centre distance (sun-planet) = module*(sunTeeth+planetTeeth)/2. Planets below ~12 teeth can show tip interference with the ring (undercut) - prefer planetTeeth >= 12. Gear ratio (sun in, ring fixed, carrier out) = 1 + ringTeeth/sunTeeth. All gears share the axis direction (default +Z); the sun and ring are centred on `position`, planets orbit it. Returns affected = [sun, ...planets, ring] and data {ringTeeth, ratio, centerDistance, ringPitchRadius, ids:{sun, planets, ring}}. The sun and planets are extrusion entities, the ring a mesh entity.

axis.description: Direction of the gear axis in world space. Default "z" (gears lie in the XY plane).

faceWidth.description: Thickness of every gear along the axis, > 0.

module.description: Gear module (metric), > 0, shared by sun, planets and ring.

planetCount.description: Number of planets, integer in [1, 12]. (sunTeeth + ringTeeth) must be divisible by it.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the sun/ring on the axis (z = bottom face). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Pressure angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Default 0.3491 (20°).

ringOuterRadius.description: Outer radius of the ring gear rim, >= ring pitch radius + 2.25*module (the command reports the minimum).

name: add_planetary_gearset

description: Grade a flat building pad (platform) into an existing-ground surface. Give the pad outline `boundary` (plan polygon, >= 3 simple [x, y] vertices inside the surface) and the finished level `elevation`, both in document units. Cut and fill batters (side slopes, horizontal per 1 vertical; defaults 1.5 cut, 2 fill) are projected to the ground, producing the pad, its daylight line and cut / fill volumes. Returns data { platformId, cutM3, fillM3, netM3 }. Edit later with update_platform; find the balancing level with balance_platform.

boundary.description: Closed pad outline in plan (>= 3 vertices, simple polygon; any winding).

items.description: Pad outline vertex [x, y].

cutSlope.description: Cut batter, horizontal per 1 vertical. Default 1.5.

fillSlope.description: Fill batter, horizontal per 1 vertical. Default 2.

name: add_platform

description: Cut a pocket into a planar face of a 3D solid: a closed outline (rectangle or polygon) whose vertical corners are rounded by cornerRadius (exact arcs) and whose floor edges may carry a floorFillet (exact kernel only). Give exactly one of depth, through=true (cut through the part) or upToFace (stop at the plane of a parallel planar face below). islands are closed polygons inside the outline that stay as material posts (their corners are rounded by cornerRadius too). The pocket must stay inside the picked face unless open=true (it may then run out over a side of the part, e.g. a step). The face is picked by a world point (face.near); coordinates are [u, v] in the face frame (origin = the world origin projected on the face plane, u = world X (or Y) projected on it, v = normal x u) or, with pointsFrame "world_xy", world [x, y]. All lengths are in the document length unit. cornerRadius must be >= floorFillet and >= toolDiameter / 2 for machinable corners (check_machining reports it). Consumes target, creates one mesh entity. Refusals carry error.code: FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_FACE_NOT_PLANAR, FTR_PROFILE_NOT_CLOSED, FTR_POCKET_CORNER_TOO_LARGE, FTR_POCKET_FILLET_GT_CORNER, FTR_POCKET_DEPTH_EXCEEDS_STOCK, FTR_HOLE_POINT_OUTSIDE_FACE (outline leaves the face without open=true), FTR_POCKET_ISLAND_INVALID, FTR_UP_TO_TARGET_INVALID, FTR_NEEDS_EXACT_KERNEL (floor fillet), FTR_FEATURE_BUILD_FAILED. Next: check_machining, recognize_features.

cornerRadius.description: Radius of every vertical outline corner (convex and concave), in document length units; 0 = sharp. Give it explicitly.

depth.description: Pocket depth below the face, in document length units; must be inside the stock. Omit with through=true or upToFace.

face.description: The planar face to cut into, picked by a world point.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on the planar face, in document length units.

floorFillet.description: Radius of the fillet between floor and walls, in document length units; 0 = sharp floor; must be <= cornerRadius. Needs an exact kernel.

islands.description: Optional material posts left standing inside the pocket: each a closed polygon of >= 3 [u, v] vertices (same pointsFrame as the outline), simple, fully inside the outline and not overlapping another island, in document length units.

open.description: true = the outline may leave the picked face (the pocket runs out over a side of the part); it must still overlap the face. Default false.

outline.description: Closed pocket outline on the face plane, before corner rounding.

center.description: Rectangle only: centre [u, v] in the pointsFrame, in document length units.

kind.description: "rectangle" (center + size, axis-aligned in the face frame) or "polygon" (points).

points.description: Polygon only: at least 3 vertices [u, v] (pointsFrame), in document length units; implicitly closed, simple (no self-crossing).

size.description: Rectangle only: [width along u, length along v], in document length units.

pointsFrame.description: Coordinates of the outline and islands: "face" (default) or "world_xy".

target.description: Id of the 3D solid to cut (a primitive or a kernel result).

through.description: true = cut through the whole part along the face normal (no depth, no floorFillet).

toolDiameter.description: Planned cutter diameter, in document length units; recorded for check_machining.

upToFace.description: Stop the floor at the plane of this planar face, which must be parallel to the picked face and below it. Omit depth / through.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on the planar target face, in document length units.

name: add_pocket

description: Generate a pre-engineered steel hall (factory / warehouse) in one step: portal frames every baySpacing along Y (columns + pitched rafters spanning X; several spans side by side with spans: [...]), gable posts, purlins and side rails, X-bracing in the end bays (roof and walls), pad footings under every column, roof / wall / gable cladding, a ground slab and optionally an overhead crane runway on brackets. All sizes in document units, roofPitch in degrees. Eaves haunches (10 % of the span by default; haunch option: eavesLength / apexLength as span fractions) are part of the frame analysis. Defaults: 24 m span, 48 m long, 6 m bays, 7 m eaves, 6° roof, HEA400 columns, IPE450 rafters. The defaults are a starting model, not a design: the standard end-plate connections (M20) fail check_portal_frames on a 24 m hall under snow, and a crane (10 t, rail 6 m) with pinned bases fails the rail-level sway limit h/400 — run design_portal_frames (sizes bolts, sections and, when sway governs, fixes the column bases) or set columnBase: 'fixed' before checking.

basePlates.description: Base plates with 4 M24 anchor bolts under every column. Default true.

baySpacing.description: Target frame spacing; adjusted to divide the length, in document units. Default 6000 mm.

cladding.description: Roof, side and gable cladding. Default true.

columnBase.description: Column base fixity: 'pinned' (default) or 'fixed' (rotation restrained in the frame analysis: stiffer sway, base moments in the reactions and footing / base plate M+N checks; requires basePlates; size the plates with design_portal_frames).

connections.description: Bolted end-plate moment connections (haunched eaves, apex). Default true.

crane.description: Optional crane runway on both sides: { capacity (t), railHeight, profile }.

railHeight.description: Top of runway beam (must be below the eaves).

eaveHeight.description: Column height to the eaves, in document units. Default 7000 mm.

footings.description: Pad footings under columns. Default true.

haunch.description: Rafter haunches of the moment connections (needs connections). The frame analysis (check_portal_frames / design_portal_frames) models them as stepped segments with the increased inertia and section modulus of the built-up section. Omitted: eaves haunch of 10 % of the span, no apex haunch.

apexLength.description: Apex haunch length on each rafter at the ridge, as a fraction of the span, 0–0.25 (duopitch only; the same cut-from-the-section haunch under both rafters). Default 0 = none. eavesLength + apexLength must not exceed 0.4.

eavesLength.description: Eaves haunch length along the rafter as a FRACTION OF THE SPAN, 0–0.25 (e.g. 0.1 = 10 % of the span; the haunch is cut from the rafter section, depth = rafter depth at the column face so the section there is about twice the rafter depth). 0 = no eaves haunch.

length.description: Hall length (Y), in document units. Default 48000 mm.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

purlinSpacing.description: Along the slope, in document units. Default 1800 mm.

railProfile.description: Side rails. Default C200x75x2.5 (passes check_purlins at qp 0.6 on 6 m bays).

railSpacing.description: Vertical, in document units. Default 1800 mm.

roofType.description: Roof shape: 'duopitch' (default: ridge mid-span, eaveHeight at both column lines) or 'monopitch' (one rafter per span rising at roofPitch from the low eaves at the left (x = origin, height eaveHeight) to the high eaves on the right; the columns get different heights, with several spans the slope continues across the internal column lines; no apex connection, two eaves connections per frame; wind with EN 1991-1-4 Tab. 7.3a monopitch coefficients).

span.description: Clear span between column axes (X), in document units. Default 24000 mm.

spans.description: Multi-span hall: widths of side-by-side spans along X (internal columns on shared lines, valley between roofs). Overrides span.

name: add_portal_frame_building

description: Load a revolute joint with a propeller's aerodynamics for simulate_motion (static / take-off condition, no forward speed). With n = rev/s and D = diameter (m): thrust T = Ct·ρ·n²·D⁴ (pushes the spinning body along thrustDirection), shaft power P = Cp·ρ·n³·D⁵, drag torque Q = P/(2πn) against the rotation. Ct, Cp come from propeller test data (static): typical fixed-pitch wooden / composite props Ct 0.08–0.14, Cp 0.04–0.08 (larger pitch → larger Cp). Use the PROPELLER joint (after any reduction gear). Returns the propeller id in affected[0].

id.description: Optional explicit propeller id.

joint.description: Revolute joint the propeller turns on.

thrustDirection.description: World direction of the thrust on the propeller (the pull direction), e.g. [0, 1, 0].

name: add_propeller

description: Create a pyramid solid with a rectangular base and a single apex. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. The base extends ±baseWidth/2 in X and ±baseDepth/2 in Y from the anchor point. The apex is at base-center + [0, 0, height]. All three dimensions must be > 0. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "base-center" (default) = center of the rectangular base; apex at position+[0,0,height]; "center" = geometric center of the AABB; "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB. The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin.

anchor.description: Which point on the pyramid the position refers to. "base-center" (default): center of the rectangular base; apex at position+[0,0,height]. "center": geometric center of the AABB (mid X/Y/Z). "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. Unknown values fall back to "base-center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

baseDepth.description: Full depth of the rectangular base along Y in document units. Must be > 0.

baseWidth.description: Full width of the rectangular base along X in document units. Must be > 0.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

height.description: Height from the base center to the apex along the local +Z axis in document units. Must be > 0.

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_pyramid

description: Add a rectangular bend relief to a sheet-metal part: a notch cut into the parent flat beside one end of a bend, so the bend can form without tearing. bend is the bend node id (listed in flat_pattern data.bends[].id), end 'start' or 'end' is the end of the bend line (the end the flange stops short of the edge end). width (along the bend line, beyond its end) and depth (into the parent flat from the bend tangent line) are in the document length unit; when omitted they come from the rule's relief (width = widthRatio x thickness, depth = inside radius + thickness + depthExtra) and the summary says so. The notch must fit on the free stretch of the edge. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_RELIEF_INVALID. Next: check_sheet_metal (FTR_RELIEF_MISSING), flat_pattern.

bend.description: Bend node id inside the part (e.g. "b1"), see flat_pattern data.bends[].id.

depth.description: Relief depth into the parent flat in the document length unit; > 0. Default inside radius + thickness + depthExtra from the rule relief.

end.description: Which end of the bend line gets the relief: 'start' or 'end' (the flange is narrower than the edge at that end).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

width.description: Relief width along the bend line in the document length unit; > 0. Default from the rule relief (widthRatio x thickness).

name: add_relief

description: Add a result probe to an analysis: a point (document units) at which a quantity is read from the solved results (the nearest node is used). quantity: temperature (thermal / thermo-mechanical cases, in the case temperature scale), heat_flux, u_mag / u_x / u_y / u_z (displacement), von_mises, s_xx / s_yy / s_zz (stress), and the cylindrical components s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial about an axis (axisPoint + axisDirection; default: the z axis through the centre of the mesh bounding box, so a quarter / half model needs the real axis; hoop / radial are null on the axis). Returns the probe id in affected[0].

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

axisDirection.description: Only for s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial.

axisPoint.description: Only for s_hoop / s_radial / s_axial / u_radial.

point.description: Probe location [x, y, z] in document units; it should lie on or inside a part.

quantity.description: Quantity to read at the point.

name: add_result_probe

description: Grow a rib from a planar face of a 3D solid: an OPEN polyline path (>= 2 points) is thickened by thickness (centred on the path when symmetric, else on its left), raised along the plane normal and fused to the part. plane = { origin: a point on the supporting face, normal: the OUTWARD normal of that face, which is the direction the rib rises }; the path lies on that plane in [u, v] face coordinates (origin = the world origin projected on the plane, u = world X (or Y) projected on it, v = normal x u) or, with pointsFrame "world_xy", world [x, y]. Give exactly one of height (rib height above the plane) or upToFace (stop at the plane of a parallel planar face above it). All lengths are in the document length unit. The rib must stand entirely on the face: otherwise it is refused. Consumes target, creates one mesh entity. Refusals carry error.code: FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND (no such target), FTR_FACE_NOT_PLANAR, FTR_RIB_PATH_NOT_SUPPORTED, FTR_PROFILE_NOT_CLOSED (bad path), FTR_PARAM_INVALID, FTR_UP_TO_TARGET_INVALID, FTR_FEATURE_BUILD_FAILED. Next: check_machining, inspect_topology.

height.description: Rib height above the plane, in document length units. Omit with upToFace.

path.description: Open polyline of the rib, >= 2 vertices [u, v] (pointsFrame), in document length units; consecutive vertices distinct, no self-crossing.

plane.description: The supporting plane the rib stands on and its rise direction.

normal.description: Outward normal [x, y, z] of the supporting face = the direction the rib rises; any non-zero length (normalised).

origin.description: World point [x, y, z] on the supporting planar face, in document length units.

pointsFrame.description: Coordinates of path: "face" (default), "world_xy" or "world" ([x, y, z]).

symmetric.description: true (default) = the rib is centred on the path; false = the thickness lies on the left of the path direction (in u, v).

target.description: Id of the 3D solid to add the rib to (a primitive or a kernel result).

thickness.description: Rib thickness measured across the path, in document length units; must be > 0.

upToFace.description: Raise the rib up to the plane of this planar face, which must be parallel to the plane and above it. Omit height.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on the planar target face, in document length units.

name: add_rib

description: Make a set of 3D entities move together as ONE rigid body for physics simulation (simulate_motion). Mass, centre of mass and inertia are computed from the entities' real geometry: each entity uses its assigned material (density model, else plain density), else `density` (kg/m³, default 7850 steel; aluminium 2700, wood 600, CFRP 1550). Give `massKg` when the real part mass is known (hollow parts): the distribution is scaled to it. `fixed: true` welds the body to the ground (engine block, frame, stand). A non-fixed body with no joint is a free body that falls under gravity. Next: connect bodies with add_body_joint. Returns the body id in affected[0] and its mass / centre of mass in the summary.

density.description: kg/m³ for entities without a material. Default 7850 (steel).

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D entities forming the body (e.g. a propeller: hub + 3 blades + spinner).

fixed.description: true = welded to the ground (never moves). Default false.

id.description: Optional explicit body id (shares the id space of all dynamics records).

massKg.description: Known real mass in kg; the computed mass distribution is scaled to it.

name: add_rigid_body

description: Define a room (space) with a name and number from a plan boundary polygon, or from wallIds forming a closed loop (the room then follows the inner wall faces). Draws the outline and an area tag; rooms feed the room schedule and IFC spaces. Refused if a room with the same outline already exists on the level.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

number.description: Room number. Default: level index × 100 + n (e.g. "101").

wallIds.description: Alternative to boundary: ids of walls enclosing the room (closed loop).

name: add_room

description: Add a section view to a drawing sheet: the model is cut by a plane and seen from `direction` with the cut faces hatched (hidden lines omitted). `offset` is the world coordinate of the cutting plane on the axis the view looks along (x for left/right, y for front/back, z for top/bottom); material between the plane and the viewer is removed. Pass `parentViewId` to draw the cutting-plane line with arrows and the letter on that view (the parent must show the plane edge-on, i.e. be perpendicular to `direction`, e.g. parent "front" with direction "right"). Labelled "SECTION A-A" with the next free letter. Returns the view id.

direction.description: Side the section is seen from; the cutting plane is perpendicular to this direction. No iso.

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids to draw. Omit to draw every visible 3D solid of the document (the usual choice).

offset.description: World coordinate of the cutting plane on the viewing axis (document units), e.g. 0 for the middle of a centred part.

paperPosition.description: Centre of the view on the paper in millimetres. Omit for automatic layout.

parentViewId.description: View on the same sheet that gets the cutting-plane line. Its entities are reused.

scale.description: Own scale denominator N of 1:N. Omit to use the sheet scale.

name: add_section_view

description: Cut a hole through ONE flat of a sheet-metal part. Give the shape ONE of three ways: `profileId` (a closed rectangle / closed polyline / circle drawn earlier on a plane PARALLEL to the flat), or `circle` { center, radius }, or `polygon` { points } given directly as WORLD points [x, y, z] that are projected normal onto the flat (no drawing needed; this is the way to cut a flange, whose plane is vertical or tilted: e.g. on a flange standing on the y = 0 edge of a part, with face.near [100, 0, 20], circle center [100, 0, 20] radius 4 cuts a hole 20 above the bend). A drawn profile on a flange needs its plane rotated onto the flange (rotate_entity, radians); circle/polygon avoid that. The cut is normal to the flat: the shape is projected onto the flat picked by the world point `face.near` (any point on or within one thickness of the flat), stored in the flat's own coordinates and appears as a cutout (CIRCLE for a circle) in flat_pattern and the DXF. The profile must lie wholly inside that flat and not touch other cutouts. All lengths are in the document length unit. Refusals: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PROFILE_NOT_CLOSED, FTR_FACE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_CUTOUT_INVALID. Next: check_sheet_metal (hole-to-bend and hole-to-edge distances), flat_pattern.

circle.description: Round hole in world coordinates, projected normal onto the picked flat. Use instead of profileId.

center.description: World point [x, y, z] of the hole axis (document length unit); projected onto the flat plane.

radius.description: Hole radius in the document length unit; > 0.

near.description: World point [x, y, z] on or near the flat to cut (document length unit).

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

polygon.description: Closed polygon (3+ vertices, any winding) in world coordinates, projected normal onto the picked flat. Use instead of profileId.

points.description: Polygon vertices as world points [x, y, z] (3 or more).

items.description: World point [x, y, z] of a vertex (document length unit); projected onto the flat plane.

profileId.description: Id of a closed 2D profile entity (rectangle, closed polyline or circle) on a plane parallel to the flat. Omit when giving circle or polygon.

name: add_sheet_cutout

description: Create a sheet-metal part from a closed 2D profile (rectangle or closed polyline drawn with draw_rectangle / draw_polyline) and a rule from create_sheet_metal_rule. The profile becomes the base flat of the rule's thickness on its work plane (side up = material on the +normal side, down = on the -normal side, mid = centred). Returns the part id (also the id of the derived, read-only folded solid). Lengths are in the document length unit. Refusals: FTR_RULE_NOT_FOUND, FTR_PROFILE_NOT_CLOSED (open, self-intersecting, or not a rectangle/closed polyline). Next: add_flange, add_sheet_cutout, flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

profileId.description: Id of a closed 2D profile entity (rectangle or closed polyline). It stays in the document.

rule.description: Name of a rule created with create_sheet_metal_rule; it supplies thickness, radius and K-factor.

side.description: Where the material lies relative to the profile plane: 'up' (+normal), 'down' (-normal) or 'mid' (centred).

name: add_sheet_metal_base

description: Add a floor, roof or foundation slab whose TOP sits at the level elevation + offset. Give either a plan boundary polygon or wallIds forming a closed loop (edge at the wall centerlines by default, see wallFace). Refused if a slab with the same outline, offset and role already exists on the level.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

offset.description: Top-of-slab offset from the level elevation. Default 0 (roof: put it on the level above).

role.description: Slab role used in schedules and IFC. Default floor.

thickness.description: Slab thickness (> 0), in document units. Default 200 mm.

wallFace.description: With wallIds: slab edge at the outer wall faces, the wall centerlines (default — the slab bears into the walls), or the inner faces.

wallIds.description: Alternative to boundary: wall ids forming a closed loop.

name: add_slab

description: Cut a void through a slab (stair well, lift or service shaft). Give a plan boundary polygon, or a stairId to cut its well (footprint + margin) in the floor slab of the level above — slabId is then found automatically. Openings are deducted from quantities and exported as IFC openings.

boundary.description: Opening polygon [[x, y], …], strictly inside the slab.

margin.description: With stairId: clearance around the stair footprint, in document units. Default 100 mm.

slabId.description: Slab element id, e.g. "slab-2". Optional with stairId.

stairId.description: Alternative to boundary: cut the well of this stair.

name: add_slab_opening

description: Create a sphere solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. radius must be > 0. rotation is accepted and stored for uniformity but is geometrically moot. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "center" (default) = geometric center; "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB; "base-center" = center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin.

anchor.description: Which point on the sphere the position refers to. "center" (default): geometric center. "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Radius of the sphere in document units. Must be > 0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Stored for uniformity; geometrically moot for a sphere. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_sphere

description: Create an involute spline shaft in the style of DIN 5480 (e.g. W200x5x38 = referenceDiameter 200, module 5, 38 teeth) as one extrusion along +Z (z from 0 to length). Tooth count follows DIN 5480: teeth = referenceDiameter/module - 2 (override with `teeth`). Flanks are involutes of the generating circle (module*teeth/2) at the 30° pressure angle; the nominal tooth thickness on the reference circle is half the pitch; tip radius = referenceDiameter/2 - 0.1*module, tooth depth 0.9*module (approximation of the DIN tolerances). Tooth flanks are sampled coarsely (7 points) to keep STEP/boolean cost low.

color.description: Hex color. Default "#9aa3ad".

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Centre of the bottom face. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Flank pressure angle in RADIANS, in (0, π/2). Default 0.5236 (30°, DIN 5480).

referenceDiameter.description: DIN 5480 reference diameter dB, > 0 (e.g. 200 for W200x5x38).

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: add_spline_shaft

description: Add a linear spring-damper between a point on one rigid body and a point on another body or the ground, for simulate_motion (a coil spring, a gas strut, a bungee, an engine-valve spring). Force along the line joining the two points: F = stiffness · (length - freeLength) + damping · d(length)/dt, positive = pulling the ends together; it works in any direction and for any joint arrangement (a rocker, a four-bar link, a falling body). `pointA` / `pointB` are WORLD points in DOCUMENT units at the pose the bodies are modelled in (where the spring physically attaches); each then rides on its body. `bodyA` / `bodyB` are rigid body ids (add_rigid_body) or "ground". Stiffness in N/m (1 N/mm = 1000 N/m), damping in N·s/m. The spring is relaxed at `freeLengthMm` (mm); by default that is the distance between the points at the modelled pose (no force at the start). `preloadN` instead sets the tension force at the modelled pose (positive = stretched, pulling together; negative = compressed, pushing apart), which fixes the free length = distance - preloadN / stiffness; give at most one of the two. Spring energy is part of the potential energy of simulate_motion (energy: true), and simulate_motion reports each spring's length range and force (data.springs); render_motion draws it as a zig-zag. Mass on a spring: period 2π·sqrt(m/k), static deflection m·g/k. Remove with delete_dynamics_item (also removed when either body is). Returns the spring id in affected[0].

bodyA.description: Rigid body id carrying the first end, or "ground".

bodyB.description: Rigid body id carrying the second end, or "ground".

damping.description: Viscous damping along the spring in N·s/m. Default 0.

freeLengthMm.description: Length in mm at which the spring force is zero. Default: the distance between pointA and pointB (relaxed at the start).

id.description: Optional explicit spring id (shares the id space of all dynamics records).

pointA.description: World point of the first end at the modelled pose, document units.

pointB.description: World point of the second end at the modelled pose, document units. Must differ from pointA.

preloadN.description: Alternative to freeLengthMm: tension force in N at the modelled pose (positive = stretched, pulling together; negative = compressed). Default 0.

stiffness.description: Spring rate in N/m (1 N/mm = 1000 N/m). Must be > 0.

name: add_spring

description: Create a parametric involute spur gear solid (extrusion with exact Bézier/arc tooth curves; mesh when bore > 0). Computes the full closed 2D tooth profile from module, tooth count, and pressure angle, then extrudes it by faceWidth along +Z. module (metric) sets the tooth scale: pitchDiameter = module * teeth. pressureAngle is in RADIANS; standard value is 0.3491 rad (20 degrees = Math.PI/9). faceWidth is the gear thickness along Z. bore is a central hole radius; if > 0 the gear is emitted as a closed mesh solid with a through hole (no boolean needed). position is [x, y, z] of the gear axis at its bottom face (the gear spans z..z+faceWidth, not centred on z); rotation is three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in radians (about world Z, then Y, then X). Right-handed frame, +Z up.

bore.description: Central bore hole radius in document units. >= 0 and < pitch radius. Default 0 (solid hub, extrusion entity). When > 0 the result is a mesh solid with a through hole.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#7a9cbb".

faceWidth.description: Gear face width (thickness along Z) in document units. Must be > 0. Typical: 8–12× module for spur gears.

module.description: Gear module (metric). Controls tooth scale: pitchDiameter = module * teeth. Must be > 0. Common values: 1 (small), 2 (medium), 4 (large).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the gear axis at its BOTTOM face: the gear axis passes through [x, y] and the gear spans z..z+faceWidth (it is not centred on z). Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pressureAngle.description: Pressure angle in RADIANS. Must be in (0, π/2). Standard value: 0.3491 rad (20°). Omit to use the 20° default.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

teeth.description: Number of teeth. Must be an integer >= 3. Below ~17 teeth undercut occurs; the profile is approximated by clamping the involute to the root circle.

name: add_spur_gear

description: Add a reinforced-concrete-style stair climbing one full level, modelled as a waist slab (sloping slab, waistThickness) with the steps on top; the last riser lands on the upper floor, so N risers give N-1 treads (N-2 treads + the landing when a landing is used) and every stair rises from the base of its level. Riser count defaults to the level height ÷ 175 mm (rounded up), so risers are equal; tread default 280 mm. By default it is ONE straight flight of N-1 treads, run (N-1) x tread. INTERMEDIATE LANDING: pass landingAt (riser number after which a horizontal landing slab, as thick as the waist, sits; integer 2 to N-2) and/or shape. shape "straight" (default) puts the landing in line between two flights; "quarter_turn" is an L: the second flight leaves sideways from the far end of the landing; "half_turn" is a dog-leg: the second flight doubles back beside the first, flightGap apart (default 100 mm), sharing the landing. turn "left" (default) or "right" is the side the second flight goes to (quarter_turn, half_turn). Shapes quarter_turn / half_turn without landingAt put the landing at half the risers. landingLength is the landing depth along the first flight (default = width). The start point and angle are those of the FIRST flight (middle of its first riser); the second flight is placed from the landing, and the stair is one element (one id, one mark, one takeoff line; flights and landing are separate entities stair-1:flight-1, :flight-2, :landing). The summary reports the Blondel rule (2R + G, comfortable between 600 and 650 mm) and, for a landing, a WARNING when landingLength < width plus the headroom between the landing and the floor above; add_slab_opening { stairId } cuts a well covering every flight and the landing. Refused above 200 risers, with a landing on fewer than 4 risers, or if a stair with the same start and angle already exists on the level.

angle.description: Run direction of the first flight in radians, counter-clockwise from +X. Default 0 (climbs toward +X).

flightGap.description: half_turn only: clear gap between the two flights, in document units (>= 0). Default 100 mm.

landingAt.description: Number of risers climbed before the intermediate landing (integer, 2 to riserCount - 2): flight 1 has landingAt risers, the last one arriving on the landing; flight 2 the remaining ones. Omit for no landing (unless shape is quarter_turn / half_turn, which default it to half the risers).

landingLength.description: Landing depth along the first flight direction, in document units (> 0). Default = stair width. Below the width gives a warning. Needs a landing.

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

riserCount.description: Total number of risers over both flights (integer, 2 to 200). Default: level height ÷ 175 mm, rounded up.

shape.description: Plan layout around the landing: "straight" (default, in line), "quarter_turn" (L, 90 degrees) or "half_turn" (dog-leg, 180 degrees, two flights side by side).

start.description: Plan point [x, y] at the middle of the first riser of the first flight.

treadDepth.description: Tread (going) depth, in document units. Default 280 mm.

turn.description: Side the second flight departs to for quarter_turn / half_turn, seen walking up the first flight. Default left.

waistThickness.description: Thickness of the sloping waist slab under the steps, perpendicular to the flight, in document units (> 0). Also the thickness of the landing slab. Default 175 mm.

width.description: Stair width (each flight), in document units. Default 1000 mm.

name: add_stair

description: Add a steel member with a catalogue section (e.g. "HEA300", "IPE400", "CHS76.1x3.6") between two 3D points [x, y, z] (z above the level). Role sets the layer, mark and IFC class: column, rafter, beam, brace, purlin, rail (side rail / girt) or crane (runway beam). Section depth points up for beams and along +X for vertical columns (roll π/2 turns it along +Y); roll (radians) turns it about the axis. Beams may declare startJoint / endJoint "rigid" (moment connection to the column they frame into; default pinned) and columns baseFixity "fixed" (column foot restrains rotation; default pinned or the base plate fixity): check_steel_members analyses rigidly connected beams and columns as planar moment frames. Refused if an identical member (section, role, roll, end points in either direction) already exists on the level.

baseFixity.description: Columns only: "pinned" (default; or the fixity of its base plate) or "fixed" (the foot restrains rotation in check_steel_members).

end.description: Axis end [x, y, z]; [x, y] means z = 0.

endJoint.description: Beams only: joint at the end end: "pinned" (default) or "rigid".

levelId.description: Level id. Default: the active level (a "Level 0" is created if none).

note.description: Note carried to the member schedule.

roll.description: Section rotation about the axis, radians. Default 0.

start.description: Axis start [x, y, z], z relative to the level; [x, y] means z = 0.

startJoint.description: Beams only: joint at the start end: "pinned" (default) or "rigid" (moment connection to the column it frames into).

name: add_steel_member

description: Create a freeform solid as a Catmull-Clark subdivision surface over a coarse polygon control cage — for organic shapes no primitive gives (saddles, shifter hoods, grips, dropouts, fairings, handles). Start from a `box` cage (size + segments per axis) or a `cylinder` cage (radius, height, sides, segments along Z), both centred on `position`, or give a custom closed cage (`vertices` local to `position` + `faces` as vertex-index loops wound counter-clockwise seen from outside). Then shape it with edit_subdivision_cage (move / scale regions of cage vertices, with soft falloff; crease edges). The surface stays inside the cage and is smooth (2-3 levels); creased edges stay sharp. Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices } (cage vertices in world coordinates, by index) to aim later edits. A closed solid: booleans, blend_union, measurement and export all work. With the OCC kernel a smooth solid (levels >= 1) is an exact B-spline solid — one bicubic face per refined cage quad, exactly the limit surface away from extraordinary vertices and creases (close to it there) — so STEP export and booleans are exact; levels 0 stays faceted.

segments.description: Cage faces along x, y, z (1..32; default [1, 1, 1]).

size.description: Cage size [x, y, z] (> 0); the smooth surface sits inside it.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

creases.description: Cage edges kept sharp, as [vertexIndex, vertexIndex] pairs (each must be an edge of a face).

cylinder.description: Cylinder (n-gon prism) cage along Z centred on position.

height.description: Cage height along Z (> 0).

sides.description: Sides of the cage polygon (3..64; default 8).

faces.description: Custom cage faces (use with vertices); the cage must be closed.

items.description: Vertex indices of one face, counter-clockwise from outside.

id.description: Optional explicit entity id. If omitted a unique id is generated.

layerId.description: Layer id to assign the entity to. Defaults to the document default layer.

levels.description: Subdivision levels 0..4 (0 = the faceted cage itself; 2-3 is smooth; each level quadruples the face count).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World position of the cage origin. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

items.description: Cage vertex [x, y, z], local to position.

name: add_subdivision_solid

description: Attach an operating temperature limit to a part (entityId) or to faces / points (target) of a heat_* analysis; returns the limit id in affected[0]. Faces are given as points near them (facesNear, document units). amplitude names a define_amplitude curve that scales the value (sink temperature for film / radiation) over time. description: Create a torus (donut) solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. ringRadius is the distance from the torus center to the tube center (major radius); tubeRadius is the radius of the tube cross-section (minor radius). Both must be > 0; tubeRadius < ringRadius for a non-self-intersecting torus. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "center" (default) = geometric center of the torus; "min" = min-XYZ corner of the AABB; "base-center" = center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin. Orientation: pass EITHER rotation (Euler radians) OR axis [dx,dy,dz] = direction the local +Z (symmetry) axis should point in world space; axis wins when both are given and Euler angles are derived and stored.

anchor.description: Which point on the torus the position refers to. "center" (default): geometric center. "min": min-XYZ corner of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "center". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

axis.description: Optional direction [dx, dy, dz] (any non-zero length, normalized) that the primitive local +Z axis (its symmetry axis) points along in world space, e.g. [1, 0, 0] lays it along +X. When given it OVERRIDES rotation (the rotation param is ignored and the resolved Euler angles are stored). A zero-length or malformed axis is rejected as a no-op.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. The ring lies in the XY plane. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

ringRadius.description: Distance from the torus center to the center of the tube (major radius) in document units. Must be > 0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

tubeRadius.description: Radius of the circular tube cross-section (minor radius) in document units. Must be > 0. Should be less than ringRadius for a non-self-intersecting torus.

name: add_torus

description: Create a wedge solid — a right-triangular prism (ramp shape). Right-handed world frame, +Z up. size is [width, height, depth]: width = X extent; height = full height of the front face; depth = Z extent (ramp direction). The slope cuts the top-rear corner: front face is a full rectangle, back edge tapers to zero height. All size components must be > 0. anchor controls which point the position refers to: "min" (default) = lower-front-left corner of the bounding box (min-XYZ); "center" = geometric center of the AABB; "base-center" = center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). The anchor offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; rotation is then applied by the viewport about the stored origin.

anchor.description: Which point on the wedge the position refers to. "min" (default): lower-front-left corner of the bounding box (min-XYZ). "center": geometric center of the AABB. "base-center": center of the bottom face (mid X/Y, min Z). Unknown values fall back to "min". Offset is applied in the local UNROTATED frame; viewport rotates about the stored origin.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#6b8f9c".

position.description: World-space location of the anchor point [x, y, z] in document units. Right-handed frame, +Z up. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

size.description: [width, height, depth] in document units. width=X extent; height=full height at front face; depth=Z extent (ramp direction). All must be > 0.

name: add_wedge

description: Insert a window into a wall: cuts the wall between sill and head and adds the glazing. The summary warns when the opening overlaps a column in the wall line. Refused if it does not fit in the wall or overlaps another opening.

at.description: Alternative to offset: a plan point [x, y] projected onto the wall to place the opening center. Ignored when offset is given.

height.description: Opening height in document units (> 0). Default 1200 mm, limited to the wall height.

mark.description: Schedule mark, unique among windows. Default next WNn.

offset.description: Distance along the wall from its start to the opening CENTER, in document units (arc length on a curved wall). Takes precedence over at. Default: wall midpoint.

sillHeight.description: Height of the opening bottom above the wall base, in document units (>= 0). Default 900 mm.

wallId.description: Host wall element id: a straight ("wall-1") or curved ("curvedWall-1") wall.

width.description: Opening width in document units (> 0). Default 1200 mm.

name: add_window

description: Read-only aerodynamic drag force and the power to overcome it: D = ½ρV²·CdA, P = D·V. Give exactly one area source: `cdA` (m², e.g. a cyclist 0.21-0.27), `cd` + `referenceAreaM2`, or `cd` + `entityIds` (frontal area measured on the model, see frontal_area). Air from the standard atmosphere at `altitudeM` (default sea level, 1.225 kg/m³) or `densityKgM3`. Optional flat-plate skin friction: `frictionModel` (laminar_blasius, turbulent_power_law, turbulent_prandtl_schlichting, ittc_1957) with `wettedAreaM2` (or the wetted area of entityIds) and `lengthM` (Reynolds length) adds Cf·q·S_wet. Cd is never defaulted: take it from tests or references (flat plate normal to flow 1.28, sphere ~0.47 at Re 1e4-2e5).

altitudeM.description: Geometric altitude in m for the U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 (-5000..86000). Default 0 (sea level) unless densityKgM3 is given.

cd.description: Drag coefficient Cd (> 0) on referenceAreaM2 or on the frontal area of entityIds.

densityKgM3.description: Air density in kg/m³ (> 0) instead of the standard atmosphere, e.g. a measured value.

entityIds.description: Solids whose frontal area is the reference area (with cd).

flowDirection.description: Direction the air moves relative to the body [x, y, z] (any length, not zero). Default [1, 0, 0]: a body moving along -x.

frictionModel.description: Add flat-plate skin friction with this mean Cf correlation (needs lengthM and a wetted area).

lengthM.description: Reynolds length in m (body length along the flow) for skin friction and the Reynolds number.

resolution.description: Silhouette grid cells along its larger extent, 50..2000. Default 400 (area error ~ ±0.5 %).

speedUnit.description: Unit of speed: m/s (default), km/h, kn (knot, 1852 m/h) or mph.

temperatureOffsetK.description: ISA temperature deviation ΔT in K at the standard pressure (e.g. 15 for ISA+15). Default 0.

viscosityPaS.description: Dynamic viscosity in Pa·s with densityKgM3; default Sutherland at 288.15 K + temperatureOffsetK (1.7894e-5 Pa·s).

wettedAreaM2.description: Wetted area in m² for skin friction (default: wetted area of entityIds).

name: aero_drag

description: Move every entity in targetIds so that its bounding-box edge (or center) along the specified axis matches the reference entity's. edge values: "min-x", "min-y", "min-z", "max-x", "max-y", "max-z", "center-x", "center-y", "center-z". The reference entity is not moved. Returns affected: targetIds.

edge.description: Which bounding-box face or center to align along: "min-x"|"min-y"|"min-z"|"max-x"|"max-y"|"max-z"|"center-x"|"center-y"|"center-z".

referenceId.description: Id of the entity whose bounding-box edge is the alignment target. Not moved.

targetIds.description: Ids of entities to move. Must all exist in the document.

name: align

description: Station-by-station report of an alignment (metres): x, y, ground, design, cut/fill (design - ground, + = fill), cross-section cut / fill areas (m2, need profile + road section + surface), cumulative cut / fill volumes (m3, average-end-area method) and the mass-haul ordinate (cum. cut - cum. fill, no bulking). Also `data.csv`. With `designSpeedKmh` it checks horizontal curve radii against R = V^2 / (127 (e + f)) with e = the set_superelevation maxRate (0 plus a warning when none is set) and f from a simple speed table (0.28 at 30 .. 0.09 at 120 km/h), and vertical curve K against minimum crest / sag K (AASHTO-style stopping sight distance table), plus grade breaks over 0.5 % without a vertical curve; failures are listed.

designSpeedKmh.description: Design speed (km/h, > 0) to enable the geometric checks.

interval.description: Row spacing, document units. Default: the alignment station interval.

name: alignment_report

description: Declare that two parts are MEANT to overlap (a press fit, a thread, a weld, or an overlap by design), so check_assembly reports the pair as FPR_PAIR_ALLOWED (pass, with your reason shown) instead of FPR_PAIR_HARD. Welds, threads and press fits also count as rigid connections when check_assembly decides whether a part is attached (FPR_PART_FLOATING). The declaration is stored in the document, is never applied silently and is listed in every check. Refused when a = b, an id is unknown or 2D, the reason is empty, or the pair already has an intent (remove_interference_intent first). Returns the intent id (fit-<step>.<k>) in affected[0]. Next: check_assembly.

a.description: Entity or instance id of the first part.

b.description: Entity or instance id of the second part (different from a).

reason.description: Why the overlap is intended, e.g. "pin pressed into piston boss, 0.02 mm interference". Must be non-empty.

name: allow_interference

description: Read-only inviscid analysis of a 2D airfoil section: linear-strength vortex panel method with the Kutta condition (Kuethe & Chow), giving lift cl, pitching moment cm about `momentReference` (fraction of chord, default 0.25) and the pressure distribution Cp; plus thin-airfoil theory (zero-lift angle, cm c/4) for NACA sections. Give `naca` ("2412") or `entityId` of a closed 2D polyline (chord along its local x; any size). `alphasDeg` angles of attack in degrees (default [0, 5]); lift slope and zero-lift angle are fitted from them. Inviscid: no drag, no stall, no Reynolds effect — real sections reach about 85-95 % of the inviscid lift slope below stall (NACA 0012 measured 0.106/deg vs 0.1195 here). `includeSurface` returns Cp per panel. Next: analyze_wing with the section lift slope and zero-lift angle.

alphasDeg.description: Angles of attack in degrees, each within -20..20, at most 41. Default [0, 5].

closedTrailingEdge.description: NACA only: sharp closed trailing edge (default true).

entityId.description: Id of a closed 2D polyline airfoil (e.g. from draw_naca_airfoil). Give this or naca.

includeSurface.description: Return x/c, y/c, Cp, V/V∞ per panel for every angle. Default false.

momentReference.description: Moment reference point as a fraction of chord. Default 0.25.
