Only a human-held signature over the payload verifies (09 PLM signing port): an agent has none and gets THM_HUMAN_GATE with the document unchanged. Do not try to work around it: hand the row over to the reviewer, who dispositions it in the desktop app. The disposition binds to the results hash and ends when the case is solved again.

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

signature.description: Human signature object from the signing port. Agents cannot produce one.

name: dispose_thermal_limit

description: Distribute 2 or more entities evenly along a single axis. mode="equal-spacing" (default): center-to-center step is uniform. mode="equal-gap": gap between AABBs is uniform. The first and last entity (by their current position along the axis) are the anchors and are not moved; all entities in between are repositioned. Returns affected: the ids of the entities that actually moved.

axis.description: Axis along which to distribute: "x", "y", or "z".

mode.description: "equal-spacing" (default): equal center-to-center distance. "equal-gap": equal gap between entity bounding boxes.

targetIds.description: Ids of entities to distribute. Must contain at least 2 existing entity ids.

name: distribute

description: Manhole and pipe schedules as CSV: ids, names, coordinates, rim and invert levels, depth, diameter, length, slope and material (metres). Returns data { manholeCsv, pipeCsv, csv }.
name: drainage_schedule

description: Draw a circular arc or a full circle in the local 2D work plane, defined by center and radius (and start/end angles in radians for an arc). Angles are measured counter-clockwise from the +X axis. radius must be > 0. The arc sweeps CCW from startAngle to endAngle (endAngle < startAngle wraps around CCW); a sweep larger than 2π is wrapped into (0, 2π] and the summary says so. OMIT BOTH startAngle and endAngle to draw a full circle (a `circle` entity, id circ-*); give both for an `arc` entity (id arc-*).

center.description: Center point [x, y] of the arc in local 2D work-plane coordinates.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

endAngle.description: End angle in radians, measured counter-clockwise from the +X axis. Arc sweeps from startAngle to endAngle counter-clockwise. Omit together with startAngle for a full circle.

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radius.description: Arc radius. Must be greater than 0.

startAngle.description: Start angle in radians, measured counter-clockwise from the +X axis. E.g. 0 = rightmost point. Omit together with endAngle for a full circle.

name: draw_arc

description: Compute the closed centerline of a belt or chain wrapping ≥2 circular pulleys/sprockets and emit it as a single closed polyline entity. For each adjacent pair of pulleys the command computes the external common tangent (open-belt / same-direction rotation convention, CCW outer envelope), then samples the wrap arc on each pulley between the two tangent touch-points. The result is one `polyline` with `closed: true`. pulleys is an ordered array of {center:[x,y], radius} objects; the belt wraps them in that order and closes back to the first. arcSamples controls chord resolution per wrap arc (default 12, minimum 2). position/rotation place the entity in 3D world space (default [0,0,0]). Fails gracefully (no-op) when: fewer than 2 pulleys, non-positive or non-finite radius, non-finite center coordinates, coincident centers, or any pulley is contained inside another (no external tangent exists).

arcSamples.description: Integer number of chord segments used to approximate each pulley wrap arc. Must be >= 2. Default 12. Higher values give smoother arcs.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

pulleys.description: Ordered list of pulleys the belt wraps around. Each entry is an object { center: [x, y], radius: number } where center is a 2D point in the work plane and radius is a finite positive number. The belt wraps them in the given order and closes back to the first. Minimum 2 pulleys.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X) for the work plane. Defaults to [0,0,0].

name: draw_belt_around

description: Draw an axis-aligned ellipse in the local 2D work plane, defined by center and semi-axis radii. radiusX is the half-width along the local X axis; radiusY is the half-height along the local Y axis. Both must be > 0. position places the work-plane origin in 3D space (default [0,0,0]).

center.description: Center point [x, y] of the ellipse in local 2D work-plane coordinates.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

radiusX.description: Semi-axis length along the local X axis (half-width). Must be greater than 0.

radiusY.description: Semi-axis length along the local Y axis (half-height). Must be greater than 0.

name: draw_ellipse

description: Draw an open 2D involute curve sampled as a polyline in the local work plane. The involute of a circle: x(t) = baseRadius*(cos t + t*sin t), y(t) = baseRadius*(sin t − t*cos t). baseRadius is the base circle radius (must be > 0). startAngle and endAngle are the involute parameter t at the curve start and end (endAngle must be > startAngle). samples is the number of points on the curve (minimum 2; default 24). At t=0 the curve originates at (baseRadius, 0); radial distance from origin at t is baseRadius*sqrt(1+t²). The curve is open (not closed) and can be fed to other commands or used standalone as a reference curve. position is [x,y,z] world-space placement of the work-plane origin (default [0,0,0]). rotation is three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in radians (about world Z, then Y, then X; default [0,0,0]).

baseRadius.description: Base circle radius of the involute. Must be > 0. Controls the curvature: smaller baseRadius gives a more tightly wound curve.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

endAngle.description: Involute parameter t at the end of the curve, in radians. Must be > startAngle. The radial distance from origin at the endpoint is baseRadius*sqrt(1 + endAngle²).

name.description: Optional display name for the entity (shown in the scene tree).

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X) for the work plane. Defaults to [0,0,0].

samples.description: Number of points sampled along the curve (inclusive of both endpoints). Minimum 2. Default 24. Higher values give a smoother polyline.

startAngle.description: Involute parameter t at the start of the curve, in radians. Defaults to 0. At t=0 the curve starts at (baseRadius, 0). Must be < endAngle.

name: draw_involute

description: Draw a NACA 4-digit (e.g. "0012", "2412", "4415") or 230-series 5-digit ("23012") airfoil section as one closed 2D polyline (NACA Report 824 ordinates, cosine spacing, upper trailing edge -> leading edge -> lower trailing edge). `chord` in document units; leading edge at `position`, chord along +x; `incidenceDeg` rotates the section nose-up about the leading edge. `closedTrailingEdge` (default true) uses the 0.1036 last thickness coefficient (sharp TE); false gives the original open TE. Next: analyze_airfoil { entityId } for lift / moment, extrude_profile for a constant-chord wing panel, loft_sections between sections for a tapered wing.

incidenceDeg.description: Nose-up rotation about the leading edge in degrees. Default 0.

position.description: Leading-edge position [x, y, z] of the sketch plane in document units. Default origin. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: draw_naca_airfoil

description: Place a point marker at the given 3D world position. The point entity has no local 2D geometry — its position is the point location.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the point. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: draw_point

description: Draw a connected sequence of line segments through an ordered list of 2D points in the local work plane. Requires at least 2 points. When closed=true the last point connects back to the first. An OPEN series of exactly 2 points is a single straight segment and creates a `line` entity (id line-*); any other series creates a `polyline` entity (id poly-*). A closed polyline can be fed to extrude_profile (id/ids) to become a 3D solid.

closed.description: When true, the last point connects back to the first point, forming a closed loop. Defaults to false.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

points.description: Ordered list of [x, y] vertices in local 2D work-plane coordinates. Minimum 2 points required.

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin. Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

name: draw_polyline

description: Draw an axis-aligned rectangle in the local 2D work plane. The origin is at the lower-left corner; width extends along +X, height along +Y. position places the work-plane origin in 3D space. Both width and height must be > 0. Drawn on the XY plane (parallel to z = position[2]); a profile for add_sheet_cutout on a flange must lie in the flange plane, so for flanges give add_sheet_cutout circle/polygon world points instead.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

height.description: Height of the rectangle along the local Y axis. Must be greater than 0.

position.description: World-space position [x, y, z] of the work-plane origin (lower-left corner). Defaults to [0,0,0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

width.description: Width of the rectangle along the local X axis. Must be greater than 0.

name: draw_rectangle

description: Draw a Catmull-Rom interpolating spline through an ordered list of 2D through-points in the local work plane. The curve passes through every point (not a control polygon). Requires at least 2 points. When closed=true the spline loops back from the last point to the first. Centripetal Catmull-Rom parameterization is used; tessellation is performed by the renderer.

closed.description: When true, the spline loops back from the last point to the first, forming a closed curve. Defaults to false.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#4a90d9".

Walls meeting at endpoints (L/T/X corners) are joined automatically; doors and windows are then hosted with add_door / add_window. A segment that duplicates an existing wall (same end points either way, same base offset, same level) is skipped and reported, so adjacent rooms can each be drawn as a closed loop sharing an edge; refused only if every segment is a duplicate.

baseOffset.description: Base offset above the level elevation, in document units. Default 0.

closed.description: Close the loop back to the first point. Default false.

height.description: Wall height above its base (document units, > 0). Default: the level height.

material.description: Material name used by quantities/cost: concrete (default), masonry, brick, block, timber, steel, gypsum…

points.description: Centerline vertices [[x, y], …], 2 to 500.

thickness.description: Wall thickness (document units, > 0). Default 200 mm.

name: draw_walls

description: Clone several entities in one step (one undo), placing each copy at original.position + offset. Group membership is not copied. Ids that do not exist are skipped and listed in the summary; if none exist nothing changes. Returns the new entity ids in affected, in the order of the (de-duplicated) input ids.

ids.description: Entity ids to duplicate (non-empty, at most 10000). Missing ids are skipped.

offset.description: Optional [dx, dy, dz] offset applied to every copy. Defaults to [0, 0, 0] (exact overlap).

params.description: New params object for the step. Must be compatible with the command named in the step (i.e. a valid params object for step.name). The document is regenerated after replacement.

stepId.description: Id of the FeatureStep whose params are to be replaced (from doc.featureHistory[*].id).

name: edit_step_params

description: Sculpt a subdivision solid (add_subdivision_solid) by editing its control cage: select cage vertices by `vertexIndices` or by a world-space `region` box (none = all), optionally with a soft `falloff` distance so neighbours follow smoothly, then `translate` them (world vector), `scale` them about `pivot` (per axis of the solid; pivot defaults to the selection centre), and/or set `crease` (true: cage edges between selected vertices turn sharp; false: smooth again). `levels` changes the refinement. Order: scale, then translate. Returns data { vertexCount, faceCount, vertices, selected } (world cage vertices; indices of fully selected vertices).

crease.description: true: make edges between selected vertices sharp; false: make them smooth.

falloff.description: Soft-selection distance (>= 0, default 0): vertices this close to the selection move partly (smoothstep).

id.description: Id of the subdivision solid.

levels.description: Subdivision levels 0..4 (0 = the faceted cage itself; 2-3 is smooth; each level quadruples the face count).

pivot.description: World-space scale centre. Default: centre of the fully selected vertices.

region.description: Select the cage vertices inside this world-space box (alternative to indices).

max.description: World-space maximum corner [x, y, z] of the selection box.

min.description: World-space minimum corner [x, y, z] of the selection box.

description: Sanity-check a slider-crank engine analytically in milliseconds, with no simulation: exact piston travel, rod angle, crank torque per newton of piston force, and with forceN the crank torque T = F·dx/dθ, rod force F/cos β and cylinder side thrust F·tan β at chosen crank angles; and the mean-torque / mean-effective-pressure / power relation (T = MEP·V_d/(4π) four-stroke, MEP·V_d/(2π) two-stroke; P = T·ω). Geometry comes from `cylinder` (an add_cylinder_pressure id: crank radius, rod length, bore and the pressure model; angles are then CYCLE angles, 0 = firing TDC, and the gas force at each angle is used) or from crankRadiusMm + rodLengthMm (+ optional offsetMm of the cylinder axis; angles are crank degrees from TDC). Units: lengths mm, force N, pressure bar, displacement cm³, speed rpm, torque N·m, power kW. Use it before simulate_motion to check the model against hand numbers: the simulated static torque and bearing forces must match these within 0.5 %. Read-only; needs no kernel or physics engine.

forceN.description: Constant force on the piston toward the crank, N: adds torque, rod force and side thrust per angle.

description: Export the document (or a subset of entities) to glTF 2.0 format. Produces a triangle tessellation in world space for every exportable 3D solid entity. 2D shape entities are silently skipped. Revolution and instance entities are fully expanded. Returns the UNCHANGED document, affected:[], and a data object with:   format ("gltf" or "glb"), triangleCount, nodeCount, materialCount,   text (glTF 2.0 JSON string — when binary=false, default),   base64 (GLB binary blob base64-encoded — when binary=true). Structure: one glTF node + mesh per entity (node.name = the entity name from set_entity_name, else its id; each child of an instance is its own node), and entities that belong to a group (group_entities) are children of a node named after the group. Node extras carry the llull entity id and kind. Meshes carry POSITION and creased smooth NORMAL attributes. One PBR material per distinct appearance: the assigned document material (color, metalness, roughness) or else the entity color, converted to linear glTF factors — ready for Blender / Cycles or any viewer. A material finish (create_material finish) embeds procedural albedo / normal / roughness PNG maps with box-projected TEXCOORD_0 (plus KHR_materials_clearcoat); text decals (add_decal) are extra alpha-blended textured meshes. The BIN buffer is inlined as a data: URI in JSON mode. In GLB mode the 12-byte header + JSON chunk + BIN chunk are packed per the glTF 2.0 spec. entityIds: omit to export all 3D entities; provide an array to export a subset. binary: false (default) → data.text contains JSON; true → data.base64 contains GLB. Does NOT modify the document.

binary.description: Output format selector. false (default): data.text contains a glTF 2.0 JSON string with the binary buffer inlined as a data: URI. true: data.base64 contains a base64-encoded GLB binary container (12-byte header + JSON chunk + BIN chunk per glTF 2.0 spec). Most web viewers accept JSON glTF; most desktop importers accept GLB.

description: Export 3D solids to STEP (AP214, ISO 10303-21) directly from the geometry kernel's exact B-rep: primitives, booleans, fillets, chamfers and shells are written as true analytic/NURBS faces, not triangles. No Python needed. Requires the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server); the default Manifold kernel gracefully no-ops (use export_step via the Python bridge, or export_stl, instead). Each solid becomes one STEP product named after its entity (set_entity_name, else the id; the group name goes in the product description) and carries its entity color as a surface style. Returns data: { format, step (the file text), solidCount (the expanded solids written), entityIds (the selected loose-solid / instance ids written, each once; never internal expanded ids), skipped, assembly? }. When the selection holds component instances (assembly parts, fasteners) the file has real assembly structure: one root product, ONE product per component (its solids written once) and one NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE per instance with its placement, named after the instance (instances sharing a name get a numeric suffix (Name 1, Name 2) so every occurrence name is unique); data.assembly = { products, occurrences }. Instances with a uniform scale share one scaled product per scale; only a non-uniform or mirrored scale is written as its own product of world-space solids named <instance>/<part> (inside a component, just that nested instance). Requires a kernel that writes assemblies (OCC); otherwise the flat list of world-space solids is written. Does not modify the document.

confirmExportControlled.description: Human confirmation for a document that uses export-controlled (ITAR / EAR) material records: a signature object produced in the desktop app, with a nonce field, over the export act and the document hash. An agent cannot give it: true is refused with MAT_HUMAN_GATE. Without it a controlled document is refused with MAT_EXPORT_CONTROLLED.

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids to export. Omit or pass [] to export every 3D solid of the document.

name: export_step_exact

description: Export the document (or a subset of entities) to STL format — the standard triangle-mesh interchange format accepted by slicers, mesh editors, and 3D printers. Produces a triangle tessellation in world space for every exportable 3D solid entity. 2D shape entities (line, polyline, arc, circle, rectangle, text, dimension, etc.) are silently skipped — STL is a solid/mesh format. Returns the UNCHANGED document, affected:[], and a data object with:   format ("ascii"|"binary"), triangleCount (number of exported triangles),   stl (ASCII STL string — when format="ascii"),   stlBase64 (base64-encoded binary STL bytes — when format="binary"). Supported entity kinds: box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, pyramid, extrusion, mesh. entityIds: omit to export all 3D entities; provide an array to export a subset. format: "ascii" (default, human-readable) or "binary" (more compact, required by some importers). name: optional solid name embedded in the STL header (default: the entity name when exactly one named entity is exported, else "llull"). perEntity: one named solid block per entity (ASCII). Does NOT modify the document.

confirmExportControlled.description: Human confirmation for a document that uses export-controlled (ITAR / EAR) material records: a signature object produced in the desktop app, with a nonce field, over the export act and the document hash. An agent cannot give it: true is refused with MAT_HUMAN_GATE. Without it a controlled document is refused with MAT_EXPORT_CONTROLLED.

entityIds.description: Array of entity ids to include in the export. Omit (or pass []) to export ALL 3D solid entities in the document. 2D-only entities in the list are silently skipped. Unknown ids are also silently skipped with a note in summary.

format.description: STL output format. "ascii" (default): returns data.stl as a human-readable ASCII STL string. "binary": returns data.stlBase64 as a base64-encoded binary STL blob (84-byte header + 50 bytes per triangle). Most slicers accept both; binary is more compact for large meshes.

name.description: Solid name to embed in the STL header (ASCII: "solid <name>"…"endsolid <name>"; binary: first bytes of the 80-byte header). Default: "llull". Use a meaningful name to help downstream tools identify the mesh.

perEntity.description: ASCII only: write one "solid <entity name or id>" … "endsolid" block per entity (names from set_entity_name, else the entity id) instead of one merged solid; `name` is then ignored. Default false. Binary STL has no per-solid names.

name: export_stl

description: Lengthen a line entity so one of its endpoints meets the infinite extension of a boundary line. Both id and boundaryId must be line entities. The endpoint of id that is closer to the intersection with the boundary (extended if necessary) is moved to that intersection point. No-op if lines are parallel, entities are missing or not lines, or id === boundaryId.

boundaryId.description: Id of the line entity that acts as the extend boundary.

id.description: Id of the line entity to extend.

name: extend

description: Read-only: extract the pipe in a region (one per call in this version): native cylinder fit, ends from the inliers' axial extent, and the DN snap of OD = 2 (r - insulationThickness) on llull's EN 10220 / ASME B36.10M table within toleranceMm (named default 1.5 mm). No table row within the tolerance: SCN_FIT_NO_STANDARD_SIZE and the measured OD is kept. data.extractions[] carry an `extraction` record ready for commit_asbuilt_extraction (which creates the as-built pipe run); data.rejected[] lists fits outside [minRadius, maxRadius].

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

distanceThreshold.description: Explicit inlier band in document units (default 3 x noiseSigma, else 2.5 x the median point spacing).

insulationThickness.description: Insulation thickness in document units, subtracted from the fitted radius (default 0, named).

maxRadius.description: Largest accepted pipe radius in document units (default 2 m).

minRadius.description: Smallest accepted pipe radius in document units (default 5 mm).

noiseSigma.description: Scanner noise sigma in document units, when known: inlier band 3 sigma and the CRLB at sigma.

normalThresholdDeg.description: Largest angle between a point normal and the model normal for an inlier, degrees (default 20).

seed.description: RANSAC seed (default 1); same seed = same result (AF-13).

sizeTable.description: Size table for the DN snap (default en10220).

toleranceMm.description: OD snap tolerance in mm (default 1.5, OUTSIDE_DIAMETER_TOLERANCE_MM).

name: extract_pipes

description: Extrude a closed 2D profile along +Z into an extrusion solid. Right-handed world frame, +Z up. Give EXACTLY ONE source: `profile` (inline array of [x, y] points, at least 3, implicitly closed, placed at `position`, default [0,0,0]); OR `id` of one closed drawn shape (circle, rectangle, ellipse, closed polyline, closed spline); OR `ids` of several coplanar open pieces (line, arc, open polyline, open spline) that join end to end into one closed loop, in any order and direction. A drawn sketch keeps its curved boundaries exact (true arcs and Bézier splines for the exact kernel and STEP export; the polygon is only the display tessellation), is placed at the (first) source entity position (override with `position`), does not inherit the source rotation, and stays in the document. The solid spans from the position along +Z for depth units (depth must be > 0). Orientation: pass EITHER rotation (Euler radians) OR axis [dx,dy,dz] = the extrusion direction (the profile plane normal; local +Z maps to it). axis wins when both are given; the derived Euler angles are stored.

axis.description: Optional direction [dx, dy, dz] (any non-zero length, normalized) that is the extrusion direction (local +Z) points along in world space, e.g. [1, 0, 0] lays it along +X. When given it OVERRIDES rotation (the rotation param is ignored and the resolved Euler angles are stored). A zero-length or malformed axis is rejected as a no-op.

color.description: Hex color string #rrggbb, e.g. "#c8553d". Defaults to "#c8553d".

depth.description: Extrusion depth in document units along +Z from the position. Must be > 0.

id.description: Id of one closed 2D shape: circle, rectangle, ellipse, closed polyline or closed spline. Use ids instead for a loop made of several pieces.

ids.description: Ids of coplanar 2D pieces (line, arc, polyline, spline) that join end to end into one closed loop; order and direction do not matter. Alternative to id and profile.

position.description: World-space origin of the profile plane [x, y, z] in document units. Defaults to [0, 0, 0] for an inline profile and to the (first) source entity position for id/ids. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

profile.description: Inline closed loop: array of [x, y] points in the XY plane of the profile (at least 3, do not repeat the first point). Omit when id or ids is given.

rotation.description: three.js intrinsic XYZ Euler angles in RADIANS [rx, ry, rz] (equivalent to rotating about world Z first, then world Y, then world X). Matches rotate_entity convention. Defaults to [0, 0, 0]. If non-finite or not length-3 the rotation is ignored and [0,0,0] is used.

name: extrude_profile

description: Quick fatigue life at ONE stress or strain amplitude (no FE, no document change). method stress_life: material record + modelId of an S-N model (sn_basquin, sn_power_law, sn_table) and a stress `amplitude` (+ `mean`, `meanStress` model, Marin `modifiers` that multiply the curve strength, e.g. surface 0.8). method strain_life: modelId of an en_coffin_manson model and EITHER `strainAmplitude` OR `nominal` { amplitude, mean } with an optional `notch` { kt, q, feIncludesKt } (needs cyclicModelId, a cyclic_ramberg_osgood model: Neuber local stress / strain, then CMB, Morrow or SWT life). Returns data { cyclesToFailure, reversalsToFailure, equivalentAmplitudeMPa, localStressMaxMPa, localStrainMax, transitionReversals, extrapolated, items[], unverified, reviewRequired }. An amplitude at or above Ftu returns item FAT_STATIC_FAILURE and no life. Results are not approved: a qualified engineer must review.

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

cyclicModelId.description: strain_life with nominal stress or SWT: id of the cyclic_ramberg_osgood model.

material.description: Material record id (define_material_record / create_material name) holding the models.

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

walker.description: Walker exponent gamma in (0, 1]; gamma 0.5 equals SWT.

meanStress.description: Mean-stress correction: none | goodman (needs Ftu on the record) | gerber (Ftu) | soderberg (Fty) | morrow (sn_basquin sigma_f) | swt | { walker: gamma }. A compressive mean gives no benefit for goodman / gerber / soderberg / morrow unless compressiveMean "formula". Default none.

modelId.description: Id of the S-N or en_coffin_manson model on that material (add_material_model).

modifiers.description: stress_life: Marin modifiers (surface, size, reliability ...), each with a justification.

justification.description: Mandatory reason / source of the factor.

value.description: Factor > 0 multiplying the curve strength (0.8 = 20 % weaker than the test specimen). Never defaulted.

nominal.description: strain_life: nominal stress amplitude and mean; local response by Neuber when a notch is given.

amplitude.description: A stress { value, unit } with a stress unit (MPa, ksi, psi, ...).

unit.description: Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.
Unit text of the 08 grammar, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'W/(m^2*K)', 'W'.

notch.description: Optional notch: the nominal stress is scaled by Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1) (Neuber on the cyclic curve for strain-life).

feIncludesKt.description: true when the stress already contains the concentration (no extra Kf); false: Kf scales the nominal stress.

q.description: Notch sensitivity q in [0, 1]: Kf = 1 + q (Kt - 1).

strainAmplitude.description: strain_life: total strain amplitude (> 0), alternative to `nominal`.

name: fatigue_life

description: Read the finite-element status of an analysis: data { state: unmeshed | meshed | solved | stale | missing | untrusted, unitSystem, mesh (node and element counts, quality, warnings), results (per load case max von Mises and max displacement with positions and units, or the thermal summary), problem { code, message } | null, probes [{ probeId, quantity, unit, nodeId, nodeDistance, values per load case or time }] }. Numbers are recomputed from the artifact store, never read from the document: "missing" = an artifact is not available on this machine (or no artifact store; re-run fea_mesh / fea_solve) and "untrusted" = the recorded summary differs from its artifact (FEA_SUMMARY_MISMATCH); in both cases mesh and results are null. Probe values are read at the nearest mesh node (no interpolation). Values are in the analysis unitSystem (N-mm-t-s: mm, MPa).

analysisId.description: Id of the analysis (affected[0] of create_analysis, e.g. an-1.1).

name: fea_report

description: Round a single vertex of a polyline with a tangent arc of the given radius. The polyline entity is updated: the vertex at vertexIndex is replaced by two tangent points (one on each adjacent segment), and a new arc entity is added tangent to both segments. vertexIndex is 0-based; for an open polyline valid range is 1 to N-2 (interior vertices only); for a closed polyline any vertex 0 to N-1 is valid. No-op if radius is too large for the adjacent segment lengths, or if the entity is not a polyline.

id.description: Id of the polyline entity to fillet.

vertexIndex.description: 0-based index of the polyline vertex to fillet. For open polylines: valid range is 1 to N-2 (interior vertices). For closed polylines: valid range is 0 to N-1.

name: fillet_2d

description: Round (fillet) exact B-rep edges of a 3D solid entity and replace it with a new mesh entity that keeps the exact construction (its brep recipe), so booleans, further fillets and STEP export still see true faces and edges. The source entity is consumed. Select edges with edgeIndices (indices from inspect_topology) and/or edgesNear (points near the edges, robust to parametric edits); with neither, ALL edges are filleted. Requires a geometry kernel that supports fillets (the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server)). With the default Manifold kernel, this command gracefully no-ops (returns unchanged doc). Target must be a 3D solid (box, cylinder, sphere, cone, torus, wedge, pyramid, extrusion, revolution, or mesh — including boolean results).

edgeIndices.description: 0-based indices of the unique B-rep edges to fillet, as listed by inspect_topology on the same entity (each edge counted once). Pass [] or omit (with no edgesNear) to fillet ALL edges.

edgesNear.description: Select edges by location: each point picks the roundable edge nearest to it (distance to the edge curve, so any point on an edge, e.g. its visible corner on a drawing, selects it). Prefer this in parametric models: the feature history keeps the points, so the same edge is re-selected after an upstream edit renumbers edges. Combines with edgeIndices.

items.description: A point [x, y, z] near the edge to fillet (e.g. its mid point from inspect_topology).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to fillet. Must exist and be a 3D solid kind.

radius.description: Fillet radius in document units. Must be > 0.

radiusEnd.description: Variable fillet: radius at the END of each selected edge (> 0); the radius varies linearly from radius at the edge start to radiusEnd. Omit for a constant radius.

name: fillet_edge

description: Filter entities by any combination of: kind, layerId, name (exact or substring), tag (exact), bboxMin/bboxMax (legacy overlap), nearPoint (centroid within radius), insideBBox (AABB fully inside), overlapsBBox (AABB intersects), touchingId (bbox touches another entity), nameFuzzy (case-insensitive substring on name), tagFuzzy (case-insensitive substring on any tag). All supplied filters are AND-ed. Returns matched entity descriptors (id, kind, layerId, name, tags) in result.data. Does NOT modify the document.

bboxMax.description: World-space maximum corner [x, y, z] of a bounding box filter. Must be provided together with bboxMin. Only entities whose world-space AABB overlaps this box are returned.

bboxMin.description: World-space minimum corner [x, y, z] of a bounding box filter. Must be provided together with bboxMax. Only entities whose world-space AABB overlaps this box are returned.

insideBBox.description: Spatial filter: return only entities whose world-space AABB is FULLY inside the given box. Provide as [[minX,minY,minZ],[maxX,maxY,maxZ]]. min must be <= max on every axis.

kind.description: Filter by entity kind. One of: "box", "cylinder", "sphere", "extrusion", "mesh", "cone", "torus", "wedge", "pyramid", "revolution", "sweep", "loft", "subdivision", "line", "polyline", "arc", "circle", "rectangle", "point", "ellipse", "spline", "text", "dimension", "image", "instance". Omit to match all kinds.

layerId.description: Filter by layer id. Only entities assigned to this layer are returned. Omit to match all layers.

name.description: Filter by entity name. By default performs a case-insensitive substring match. Set nameExact:true for a case-sensitive exact match. Omit to match all names.

nameExact.description: When true, the name filter requires an exact case-sensitive match instead of a substring match. Default: false.

nameFuzzy.description: Fuzzy name filter: case-insensitive substring match on entity name. Matches any entity whose name contains this string. Omit to skip this filter.

nearPoint.description: Spatial filter: return only entities whose bbox centroid is within `radius` units (3D euclidean) of `point`. Provide as { "point": [x, y, z], "radius": number }. radius must be > 0.

point.description: World-space origin [x, y, z] of the proximity search.

radius.description: Maximum distance from point to entity centroid. Must be > 0.

overlapsBBox.description: Spatial filter: return only entities whose world-space AABB INTERSECTS the given box. Provide as [[minX,minY,minZ],[maxX,maxY,maxZ]]. min must be <= max on every axis.

tag.description: Filter to entities that have this exact tag string in their tags array. Omit to match all entities regardless of tags.

tagFuzzy.description: Fuzzy tag filter: case-insensitive substring match on any tag in the entity's tags array. Matches if ANY tag contains this substring. Omit to skip this filter.

touchingId.description: Spatial filter: return entities whose world-space AABB overlaps the AABB of the entity with this id. The reference entity itself is excluded from results. The id must exist in the document.

name: find_entities

description: Clearance of a hole/shaft fit at operating temperatures. Give explicit limits for the hole and the shaft (nominal diameter and upper/lower deviations in document units, valid at specTemperature) and each part's CTE: a document material (holeMaterial / shaftMaterial = create_material name; a thermalStrain model is preferred, a cte model needs cteBasis[material] = secant with a reference temperature, or instantaneous) or an explicit secant CTE (holeCte / shaftCte with its reference temperature). specTemperature is the temperature the limits apply at and has NO default. Temperatures: `temperatures` (both parts), `range` {min, max, steps}, or per-part `holeTemperatures` + `shaftTemperatures` (same length), each with a unit. D(T) = D_spec (1 + a_sec (T - T_spec)) is applied to every limit diameter. Returns per row min/max clearance in document length units (negative = interference), a status (clearance, interference, interference_possible, clearance_possible), code TMC_FIT_INTERFERENCE / TMC_FIT_LOOSE against the fit intent (derived from the limits at specTemperature unless given), `unverified`, and the formula and CTE sources; every row needs review by a qualified engineer (disposition pending_human on failing rows). Optional `lame` adds contact pressure and hub bore hoop stress (elastic, constant E and nu). Use before approving a mixed-material fit; next: change materials / tolerances, or hand a failing row to a human reviewer.

kind.description: secant: alpha(T) is referenced to referenceTemperature; instantaneous: alpha is d(strain)/dT.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

cteBasis.description: Basis of the cte model per material name (PHY-01 models carry no basis field).

lower.description: Lower deviation from nominal in document units (e.g. 0 for H7); must not exceed upper.

nominal.description: Nominal diameter in document units (equal for hole and shaft).

upper.description: Upper deviation from nominal in document units (e.g. +0.021 for an H7 hole of 20 mm).

holeCte.description: Explicit CTE of the hole part (alternative to holeMaterial).

alpha.description: Secant CTE, unit of 1/K (e.g. { value: 23e-6, unit: '1/K' }).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

referenceTemperature.description: Temperature the secant CTE is referenced to (the datasheet statement), e.g. { value: 20, unit: "degC" }.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

source.description: Where the value comes from (recorded in provenance; it stays unverified without a material record).

holeMaterial.description: Hole part material (create_material name) whose thermalStrain / cte property model gives the CTE.

holeTemperatures.description: Hole temperatures, paired by index with shaftTemperatures (different part temperatures).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

intent.description: Intended fit; default derived from the limits at specTemperature.

lame.description: Adds Lame contact pressure (solid shaft in a hub) and hub bore hoop stress per row.

hubE.description: Hub Young's modulus, pressure unit, e.g. { value: 70000, unit: 'MPa' }.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

hubOuterDiameter.description: Hub outer diameter in document units (> nominal).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.
Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.
Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

steps.description: Number of temperatures, ends included (2 to 200).

lower.description: Lower deviation from nominal in document units (e.g. 0 for H7); must not exceed upper.

nominal.description: Nominal diameter in document units (equal for hole and shaft).

upper.description: Upper deviation from nominal in document units (e.g. +0.021 for an H7 hole of 20 mm).

shaftCte.description: Explicit CTE of the shaft part (alternative to shaftMaterial).

alpha.description: Secant CTE, unit of 1/K (e.g. { value: 23e-6, unit: '1/K' }).

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

referenceTemperature.description: Temperature the secant CTE is referenced to (the datasheet statement), e.g. { value: 20, unit: "degC" }.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

source.description: Where the value comes from (recorded in provenance; it stays unverified without a material record).

shaftTemperatures.description: Shaft temperatures, paired by index with holeTemperatures.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

specTemperature.description: REQUIRED, never defaulted: temperature the limits apply at, e.g. { value: 20, unit: "degC" }.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

temperatures.description: Operating temperatures applied to hole and shaft together.

unit.description: Unit, e.g. 'degC', 'K', 'degF', 'MPa', '1/K'.

name: fit_at_temperature

description: Fit a constitutive law that is linear in its parameters to test data and return the model, residuals per test and its stability (deterministic, exact QR). kind hyper_neo_hooke | hyper_mooney_rivlin | hyper_yeoh | hyper_polynomial | hyper_reduced_polynomial (order 1-3): tests with mode uniaxial | equibiaxial | planar, rows [stretch, nominal stress], xMeasure 'stretch', yMeasure 'nominal_stress', units { y: 'MPa' }; the Drucker stability scan is returned (MATL_HYPERELASTIC_UNSTABLE) and a single mode warns MATL_FIT_INSUFFICIENT_MODES. kind ramberg_osgood: one test mode 'uniaxial_plastic', rows [total strain, true stress], fixed { E, nu } (engineering form ε = σ/E + 0.002 (σ/σ0.2)^n). kind visco_prony: one test mode 'relaxation', rows [time, shear modulus], fixed { tau: [{value, unit}…], G0? } (relaxation times fixed, weights g_i fitted). Objective absolute (default, named) or relative. Nothing is added to the document: pass data.model with data.validity, basis and fit to add_material_model. Output is unverified until a data source is given and a reviewer accepts it.

dataSource.description: Where the rows come from (absent ⇒ unverified).

fixed.description: Fixed values: ramberg_osgood { E, nu } as {value, unit}; visco_prony { tau: [{value, unit}…], G0? }.

objective.description: Residual weighting: 'absolute' nominal-stress residual (default, named) or 'relative'.

rows.description: Rows [x, y] (at most 10 000 over all tests).

units.description: Units of the columns: { y: 'MPa' } (and x for time: { x: 's' }).

validity.description: Validity to attach (default: the stretch / strain / time range of the data).

data.description: [min, max] of the data the parameters were derived from.

equation.description: [min, max] the source allows (⊇ data; default = data).

unit.description: Unit of the bounds, e.g. 'K', '1/s', '1'.

variable.description: State variable the range applies to: T, strainRate, time, equivalentPlasticStrain, stretch …

name: fit_material_model

description: Read-only: fit a plane, cylinder or sphere to the cloud points of a region (native seeded RANSAC on PCA-oriented points, then Levenberg-Marquardt on the orthogonal distance, inliers re-selected until stable). data: the parameters in document units and frame, inliers, rms, coverageDeg (cylinder / sphere; below 60 deg: SCN_FIT_LOW_COVERAGE, unverified), covariance (SI), std and crlb, the named threshold, warnings, and for a cylinder an `extraction` ready for commit_asbuilt_extraction. Same seed = same result. For circles in a section use slice_cloud fit=circle.

cloudId.description: Id of an attached cloud (affected[0] of attach_point_cloud, e.g. "cloud-1.1").

distanceThreshold.description: Explicit inlier band in document units (default 3 x noiseSigma, else 2.5 x the median point spacing).

noiseSigma.description: Scanner noise sigma in document units, when known: inlier band 3 sigma and the CRLB at sigma.

normalThresholdDeg.description: Largest angle between a point normal and the model normal for an inlier, degrees (default 20).

seed.description: RANSAC seed (default 1); same seed = same result (AF-13).

name: fit_primitive

description: Fit a property law to measured rows [x, y, weight?] (at most 10 000): polynomial (degree, y vs x), log10Polynomial (NIST form, log10 y vs log10 x), arrhenius (ln y vs 1/T, x must be an absolute temperature), powerLaw (ln y vs ln x) or table1d (interpolating table). Householder QR on a scaled basis; residuals on the original y (RMS, max |r|, max |r/y|, R²); PROP_FIT_POOR above maxRelResidual (default 0.05). Returns a model that define_property_model accepts unchanged (validity = the data range, basis default unspecified ⇒ unverified until a data source is given and a reviewer accepts it). Read-only.

dataSource.description: Where the rows come from (absent ⇒ unverified).

id.description: Id of the fitted model.

objective.description: Residual weighting (default: the one the form linearises).

property.description: Catalogue property of the fitted model.

temperatureExponent.description: Fixed exponent m of arrhenius y = A T^m exp(−Q/(R T)) (default 0).

name: fit_property_model

description: Frame the entire document in the camera so all entities are visible. direction presets the viewing angle: "front" (eye at -Y looking along +Y), "back" (looking along -Y), "right" (looking along -X), "left" (looking along +X), "top" (overhead +Z), "bottom" (below -Z), "iso" (isometric, default), "current" (keep existing azimuth/polar, only adjust distance and target). padding multiplies the computed distance so geometry has breathing room (default 1.2). When the document is empty a default view is applied with an explanatory summary. Does NOT add to feature history.

direction.description: Viewing direction preset. One of: front, back, left, right, top, bottom, iso, current. Defaults to "iso". "current" keeps the existing azimuth and polar; only target and distance change.

padding.description: Scale factor applied to the computed distance so geometry is not edge-clipped. Default 1.2. Values < 1 crop the view; > 2 shows it very small. Must be > 0.

name: fit_view

description: Compute the analytic flat pattern of a sheet-metal part (BA = theta*(R+K*T) added at every bend, unfolded from the base flat) without changing the document. Returns data { extents [x, y], area, outline (vertices, bounded), bends[] with angleDeg, insideRadius, direction up/down, ba, bd, ossb and the K-factor used with its source, joggles[] with allowance/run/inclinedStraight, hems[] (add_hem: gap, returnLeg, developedLength = pi*(gap/2+K*T)+leg, unverified model; a hem bend has ossb/bd null), formingNotes[] (beads are excluded from the pattern; a flanged hole is developed to an approximate, unverified cut diameter), provenance (formulas, inputs, sources), unverified + unverifiedInputs, reviewRequired }. Lengths are in the document length unit, angles in degrees. The result is computed by llull, not approved: a qualified person must review it. Refusal: FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND, FTR_NON_DEVELOPABLE. Next: export_flat_pattern_dxf, materialize_flat_pattern, check_sheet_metal.

id.description: Sheet-metal part id (returned by add_sheet_metal_base).

name: flat_pattern

description: Read-only frontal (projected) area of 3D solids seen along the flow direction — the reference area A of drag D = ½ρV²·Cd·A — plus the wetted (surface) area for skin friction and the body length along the flow. Overlapping parts count once (silhouette union by rasterisation; `uncertaintyM2` = half the boundary cells). Lengths are converted from the document units to metres. Default flow direction [1, 0, 0]. Use for a cyclist + bike model, a fuselage, a car or any assembly; then aero_drag { cd, entityIds } or road_load_power.

entityIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids / instances to project.

flowDirection.description: Direction the air moves relative to the body [x, y, z] (any length, not zero). Default [1, 0, 0]: a body moving along -x.

resolution.description: Silhouette grid cells along its larger extent, 50..2000. Default 400 (area error ~ ±0.5 %).

name: frontal_area

description: Read a material: its record (designation, temper, form, specs, licence, export marking, superseded, library origin), every stored value (density, moduli, allowables) with unit, basis, direction, thickness / e/D / temperature condition, provenance and whether it is unverified, which value is preferred, and the density mass_properties would use. A material made with create_material is legacy: density basis unspecified, provenance legacy. A private-library record without values on this machine says unresolved. Next: get_material_allowable.

material.description: Material id (create_material name or record id).

name: get_material

description: Read one design value of a material for the EXACT key (property, basis, direction, thickness, e/D, temperature): e.g. Ftu, basis A, L, 0.050 in. A basis is never substituted: when none matches, data.available is false and data.candidates lists the values that exist (MAT_ALLOWABLE_NOT_AVAILABLE). Without temperature the room-temperature value is returned; with temperature the temperature table is interpolated linearly and refused outside its range (MAT_TEMPERATURE_OUT_OF_RANGE, no extrapolation). Every value carries basis, provenance, unverified / unverifiedReasons and reviewRequired: true: an engineer must review it. forCertification: true refuses superseded sources (MAT_SOURCE_SUPERSEDED) and typical / supplier_unstated / unspecified values (MAT_VALUE_UNVERIFIED). Add values with set_material_property.

basis.description: Required basis: A, B, S, typical, supplier_unstated, company, unspecified. Never substituted.

direction.description: Direction of the value (L, LT, ST, …); omit or isotropic for a direction-free value.

edOverD.description: Bearing edge-distance ratio e/D (1.5 or 2.0) for Fbru / Fbry.

forCertification.description: Refuse superseded sources and unverified values (default false).

property.description: Property: Ftu, Fty, Fcy, Fsu, Fbru, Fbry, E, Ec, G, nu, density, elongation, cte, k, cp.

temperature.description: Temperature for a temperature-dependent value; omit for the room-temperature value.

unit.description: Temperature: unit, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'degF', 'degC', 'K'.

thickness.description: Thickness the value must cover; needed for a value tabulated per thickness range.

unit.description: Product thickness: unit, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'degF', 'degC', 'K'.
Unit of the answer (default: the stored unit), e.g. 'MPa'.

name: get_material_allowable

description: Create a named group containing >= 2 existing entities. The group id is returned in affected. Entities are not moved or changed.

ids.description: Array of entity ids to include in the group. Must contain >= 2 ids that exist in the document.

name.description: Optional human-readable label for the group, e.g. "Wheel assembly". Defaults to "Group".

name: group_entities

description: List the holes of a part as a table for drawings: one row per hole with its label (H1, H2, ... in table order), position x, y from the top-left corner of its face (x along the face, y downwards, document length units), kind (simple, counterbore, countersink, counterdrill), diameter, countersink diameter / included angle in degrees / depth, counterbore diameter / depth, blind depth or through, drill point angle with its source (a drill point that was not given is reported as defaulted, 118 degrees, source R8) and tip height, and the cosmetic thread, and at = the hole centre [x, y, z] in world coordinates (to mark it on the model). Holes come from add_hole, or are recognised from the B-rep of an imported solid when the kernel is exact (without a kernel only authored holes are listed, otherwise FTR_NEEDS_EXACT_KERNEL). Rows are sorted by face, then y, then x. Pass origin to measure from another datum of the face frame. Lengths in the document length unit, angles in degrees. The table is returned in data = { origin, rows } plus the unit, provenance and reviewRequired (computed by llull, not approved).

id.description: Id of the 3D solid.

origin.description: Datum [u, v] in the face frame, in document length units, replacing the default top-left corner of each face.

name: hole_table

description: Turn the holes recognised on an exact 3D solid (an imported STEP part, see recognize_features) into a build_project plan of add_hole steps: data.actions, one step per group of identical holes (same kind, diameters, depth, drill point and entrance plane) with their world positions. The first step cuts into `stock`, the entity or "$alias" you will drill (a plain stock whose faces contain the hole entrances); each next step cuts into the previous result. Lengths are in the document length unit, angles in degrees; a blind hole always carries its drill point angle (0 = flat). Holes whose classification is ambiguous are included and listed in data.ambiguous. Needs an exact kernel: otherwise refused with FTR_NEEDS_EXACT_KERNEL (also FTR_PART_NOT_FOUND). Next: build_project with data.actions.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid (mesh with an exact B-rep) whose holes are read.

stock.description: Entity id (or "$alias" of an earlier plan step) of the solid the plan drills; the first add_hole step targets it.

name: holes_from_recognition

description: Convert points read off an image underlay (pixel coordinates) into model coordinates. Returns `data.world` ([x, y, z] per point) and `data.xy` ([x, y] per point — ready for draw_polyline, extrude_profile or revolve_profile when the underlay lies on the XY plane), plus `data.unitsPerPixel`. Calibrate first (calibrate_underlay) so the numbers are true scale. Image pixel coordinates [px, py]: origin at the TOP-left corner of the picture, +px right, +py DOWN (as read off the image); fractional values are fine.

id.description: Id of the image underlay the pixel coordinates refer to.

points.description: Pixel points [[px, py], …] to convert (1..10000).

items.description: Image pixel coordinates [px, py]: origin at the TOP-left corner of the picture, +px right, +py DOWN (as read off the image); fractional values are fine.

name: image_to_world

description: Import minimum-bend-radius rows (material, temper, thickness -> minimum inside radius at a bend angle) that check_sheet_metal and sheet_metal_calc match against. Give `rows` (each row states its own units 'mm' or 'in') or `csv` text with the header material,temper,thickness,minInsideRadius,units,bendAngle,source,verification. Every row needs a source (standard/handbook and edition): a row without one refuses the whole import with FTR_TABLE_ROW_NO_SOURCE and the path rows.<i>.source. Rows are 'unverified' unless marked 'verified' (dual-review transcription); results computed from unverified rows are flagged. Rows with the same key replace the earlier ones. Next: create_sheet_metal_rule.

csv.description: CSV text with a header line: material,temper,thickness,minInsideRadius,units,bendAngle,source,verification. Give this OR rows.

rows.description: Radius rows; give this OR csv.

bendAngle.description: Bend angle in degrees the row applies to (AC 43.13-1B Table 4-6 rows apply at 90).

material.description: Material label matching the rule material (text).

minInsideRadius.description: Minimum inside bend radius, in the row's `units` (mm or in).

source.description: Mandatory provenance: standard/handbook and edition (a row without it is refused, FTR_TABLE_ROW_NO_SOURCE).

temper.description: Temper label matching the rule temper (text).

thickness.description: Sheet thickness the row applies to, in the row's `units` (mm or in).

units.description: Unit of thickness and minInsideRadius of this row: 'mm' or 'in'.

verification.description: 'verified' only after dual-review transcription from the cited source; default 'unverified'.

name: import_bend_radius_table

description: Import an ASCII DXF drawing (AutoCAD, Civil 3D, BricsCAD, QCAD, survey software exports) as editable 2D entities on their DXF layers: LINE, LWPOLYLINE (bulges as arcs), POLYLINE, ARC, CIRCLE, POINT, TEXT, MTEXT, block INSERTs (exploded) and 3DFACE (one mesh per layer). Elevations are kept as the entity plane height. Units come from $INSUNITS unless `sourceUnit` is given. Binary DXF and DWG are not supported (save as ASCII DXF). For terrain from survey DXFs use import_survey_dxf.

layers.description: Only import these DXF layers (case-insensitive). Default: every layer.

sourceUnit.description: Drawing unit when $INSUNITS is missing or wrong. Default: $INSUNITS, else the document unit.

name: import_dxf

description: Import a fastener catalogue file into the document (bolts, rivets, Hi-Lok pins, nuts and washers are all families). The file is { format: "llull-fastener-catalog", schemaVersion: 1, families: [...] }; each family has id, kind, standard, a part-number grammar (literal / code table / int fields; an int field named diameterDash selects the size), sizes (dash, nominalDiameter, thread, dims such as headDiameter, height, thickness with options), grip / length rules, licence and provenance. Every dimension needs provenance.citation or sourceId and a parsable length unit. Nothing is bundled: the user supplies the dimensions (licence flags travel with the family; licensed-no-redistribution families are refused: FAST_LICENCE_EMBED_FORBIDDEN). Next: list_fastener_families, select_fastener.

catalog.description: The catalogue file object: { format: "llull-fastener-catalog", schemaVersion: 1, title?, families: FastenerFamily[] }.

replace.description: Overwrite families whose id already exists with different content. Default false: such a clash is refused (FAST_CATALOG_CONFLICT).

name: import_fastener_catalog

description: Import a material library (format llull-material-library): records with PHY-01 values, each with basis, source, licence and export marking. Give the library object (inline, embedded libraries only), or { libraryId, version, sha256 } for a library file registered on this machine (register_material_library); a licensed library (licensed-no-redistribution) is storage private: it is read from the machine, never copied into the document file, and its records stay unresolved on a machine without the file until resolve_material_libraries. A sha256 that differs from the library content is refused (MAT_LIBRARY_HASH_MISMATCH). Imported records are read-only; assign them with assign_material. Another version of a known library needs replace: true (diff_material_libraries shows what changed).

confirmation.description: Human signature object (with a nonce), required only when replace would LOWER the export marking of the library or of a record (for example ITAR → none). An agent cannot give it: MAT_HUMAN_GATE.

library.description: The library object: { format: "llull-material-library", schemaVersion: 1, id, version, title, licence, exportMarking, storage: "embedded", sources, materials[] }.

libraryId.description: Id of a library file held on this machine (instead of library).

replace.description: Replace an already imported library of the same id (a new version); default false.

sha256.description: Expected content hash. Required with libraryId; optional check with an inline library.

name: import_material_library

description: Create mesh solids from world-space triangle data — the landing point for STEP import and for code-imported shapes that have no analytic llull primitive. Each body becomes one mesh entity (optionally named and coloured). Meshes render, measure and export but have no editable dimensions.

bodies.description: Bodies to create. Each: { positions: [x,y,z, ...] world-space numbers, indices?: [i0,i1,i2, ...] (omit for a triangle soup of 9 numbers per triangle), name?: string, color?: "#rrggbb" }.

name: import_mesh

description: Import a STEP file as exact B-rep solids (not triangles): the file is read, every solid is checked and healed (BRepCheck, ShapeFix, sewing of loose shells), stored as a content-addressed document blob and shown as one mesh entity per solid that keeps its exact shape (volumes, fillets, booleans and STEP export stay exact). Needs the exact OCC kernel (kernel_info); otherwise use import_step for a mesh. Give the file as stepBase64 or text. Lengths are converted from millimetres into the document unit. data.report lists per solid validAsRead / validAfterHeal / actions / maxToleranceMm / freeEdges / faces / faceted, the root census, skipped items and warnings (KRN_IMPORT_TOLERANCE_HIGH above kernelSettings maxImportTolerance). Refusals carry error.code: KRN_NO_EXACT_KERNEL, KRN_STEP_UNREADABLE, KRN_STEP_TESSELLATED_ONLY, KRN_STEP_NO_SOLID, KRN_HEAL_FAILED. Names and colours of the STEP are not read yet (use name).

fileName.description: Original file name, kept in the report only.

heal.description: Run shape healing (ShapeFix) on every solid at the document linear tolerance. Default true.

keepOriginal.description: Also store the STEP text as a model/step document blob for audit (large). Default false.

name.description: Entity name; several solids get a numeric suffix. Default: none.

sew.description: Sew loose shells and faces into closed solids. Default true.

stepBase64.description: The STEP file bytes, base64 encoded (ISO 10303-21 text, UTF-8/ASCII). Give exactly one of stepBase64 or text.

text.description: The STEP file as Part 21 text. Give exactly one of stepBase64 or text.

name: import_step_exact

description: Extract survey points from a topographic DXF into a point group, ready for create_surface: POINT entities, vertices of 3D polylines / elevated contours / lines (breaklines), 3DFACE corners and, optionally, numeric spot-height TEXT ("123.45" placed at the level). Filter by DXF `layers` (e.g. ["TOPO_PTS", "CONTOURS"]). Points at elevation 0 are ignored unless `keepZeroElevation`. Units from $INSUNITS unless `sourceUnit`.

keepZeroElevation.description: Keep points at z = 0. Default false.

layers.description: Only these DXF layers (case-insensitive). Default: every layer.

sourceUnit.description: Drawing unit when $INSUNITS is missing. Default: $INSUNITS, else m.

sources.description: What becomes a point: points, vertices, faces, text. Default points, vertices, faces.

name: import_survey_dxf

description: Import survey points (topographic survey, total station / GNSS export) as a named point group. Give `text` (CSV / TXT file content, one point per line; header and # comment lines skipped) in `format` PENZD (default: number, easting, northing, elevation, description), PNEZD, PENZ, PNEZ, ENZ or NEZ, and/or `points` [{ x, y, z }]. Coordinates are in `sourceUnit` (default m) and are converted to the document unit. Then build a terrain with create_surface.

coordinates.description: Coordinate frame of the input. "grid" (projected CRS) is converted to local with the site calibration (set_site_calibration) and is refused without one. Default "local".

points.description: Points given directly.

number.description: Point number / name. Default: running index.

sourceUnit.description: Unit of the coordinates in `text` / `points`. Default m.

text.description: Survey file content (comma, tab, ; or space separated).

name: import_survey_points

description: Insert a straight row of identical fastener stacks (insert_fastener_stack at each position) along from -> to with either pitch {value, unit} or count. Rivet rows are checked against the minimum pitch 3 D and edge distance 2 D (AC 43.13-1B 4-57(c)); other families use minPitch / minEdgeDistance when given. edgeDistance is the distance from the row to the plate edge as the caller knows it. A violation refuses the row (FAST_PITCH / FAST_EDGE_DISTANCE, listed in data.violations) unless allowViolations is true, which places it with warnings. Selection params as in select_fastener; needs stackIds. With pitch, the pitch is adjusted (count = round(length/pitch)+1) so the last fastener lands on `to`. Returns data.rowId, data.stackIds, data.count, data.pitchIn (actual) and data.requestedPitchIn.

allowViolations.description: Place the row although pitch or edge distance is below the minimum, reporting warnings. Default false: refuse.

axis.description: Fastener axis direction [x, y, z] pointing from the head side to the nut side. Default [0, 0, 1].

codes.description: Part-number code choices by grammar field name, e.g. { "material": "AD" } for MS20470AD4. A missing choice takes the first catalogue code and is reported.

count.description: Number of fasteners, spread evenly from `from` to `to` (1..500). Give this OR pitch.

diameterDash.description: Size dash of the family as listed by list_fastener_families (e.g. "3" for NAS6203, "4" for MS20470AD4, "8" for HL19 1/4 in).

edgeDistance.description: Distance from the fastener axes to the nearest plate edge, as { value, unit }, known to the caller (it is checked against the minimum, not measured)

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

family.description: Id of the fastener family in the document catalogue (e.g. "NAS6203-6220", "MS20470", "HL19"). Use list_fastener_families to see ids.

from.description: Axis point [x, y, z] (document units) of the first fastener.

holeDiameter.description: Hole diameter as { value, unit }; overrides the catalogue hole diameter. Required when the catalogue lists none

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

holeMode.description: Hole cut through every plate of the stack with the geometry kernel: "cut_close_tolerance" (default, diameter from the catalogue size or holeDiameter), "cut_clearance" (clearance diameter from the catalogue or holeDiameter) or "none" (no cut).

maxWasherTotal.description: Largest combined washer thickness allowed as { value, unit }. Default 1/8 in (AC 43.13-1B 7-37), reported as a defaulted rule

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

minEdgeDistance.description: Minimum edge distance for non-rivet families as { value, unit }. Rivets default to 2 D (AC 43.13-1B 4-57(c)).

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

minPitch.description: Minimum pitch for non-rivet families as { value, unit }. Rivets default to 3 D (AC 43.13-1B 4-57(c)).

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

nut.description: Optional nut family id (e.g. "MS21042") for the same diameter dash; enables the thread-protrusion check.

pitch.description: Requested spacing between fastener axes as { value, unit }; the row is divided into round(length / pitch) equal intervals so the last fastener lands on `to` (actual pitch in data.pitchIn). Give this OR count

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

rivetRounding.description: Rivet length rounding to the catalogue step: "up" or "nearest". Default: the catalogue rule (up), reported as a defaulted rule.

stackIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids (plates) every fastener of the row passes through; measured at each position along axis.

to.description: Axis point [x, y, z] (document units) the row runs towards; the last fastener is exactly here.

washer.description: Optional washer family id (e.g. "NAS1149") used to shim the gap between grip and stack.

washerSide.description: Side of the stack the shim washers go on: "nut" (default) or "head".

name: insert_fastener_row

description: Insert one fastener stack through plates: runs the select_fastener rules, cuts the hole through every plate (exact boolean with the kernel), and places the bolt/pin/rivet, shim washers and nut as instances of one component per part number (created once; geometry from the catalogue dimensions, or flagged representative placeholders that are excluded from mass). Needs stackIds + axisPoint (+ axis, head to nut direction). holeMode picks the cut; holeDiameter {value, unit} overrides the catalogue. Records the stack in the document (id fst-<step>.<k>, returned in data.stackId); bill_of_materials then lists the standard parts. Refused selections change nothing. Next: check_fastener_layout, bill_of_materials. Delete with delete_fastener_stack (holes stay: undo to restore the plates).

axis.description: Fastener axis direction [x, y, z] pointing from the head side to the nut side. Default [0, 0, 1].

axisPoint.description: Point [x, y, z] in document units the fastener axis passes through (with stackIds). Not required with stack.

codes.description: Part-number code choices by grammar field name, e.g. { "material": "AD" } for MS20470AD4. A missing choice takes the first catalogue code and is reported.

diameterDash.description: Size dash of the family as listed by list_fastener_families (e.g. "3" for NAS6203, "4" for MS20470AD4, "8" for HL19 1/4 in).

family.description: Id of the fastener family in the document catalogue (e.g. "NAS6203-6220", "MS20470", "HL19"). Use list_fastener_families to see ids.

holeDiameter.description: Hole diameter as { value, unit }; overrides the catalogue hole diameter. Required when the catalogue lists none

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

holeMode.description: Hole cut through every plate of the stack with the geometry kernel: "cut_close_tolerance" (default, diameter from the catalogue size or holeDiameter), "cut_clearance" (clearance diameter from the catalogue or holeDiameter) or "none" (no cut).

maxWasherTotal.description: Largest combined washer thickness allowed as { value, unit }. Default 1/8 in (AC 43.13-1B 7-37), reported as a defaulted rule

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

nut.description: Optional nut family id (e.g. "MS21042") for the same diameter dash; enables the thread-protrusion check.

rivetRounding.description: Rivet length rounding to the catalogue step: "up" or "nearest". Default: the catalogue rule (up), reported as a defaulted rule.

stack.description: Stack thickness to fasten (total thickness of the joined layers) as { value, unit }. Give this OR stackIds

unit.description: Length unit of the value, e.g. 'in', 'mm', 'ft'.

stackIds.description: Ids of the 3D solids (plates) the fastener passes through; their thickness along the axis is measured. Give this OR stack. Needs axisPoint.

washer.description: Optional washer family id (e.g. "NAS1149") used to shim the gap between grip and stack.

washerSide.description: Side of the stack the shim washers go on: "nut" (default) or "head".

name: insert_fastener_stack

description: Place a new InstanceEntity referencing an existing Component definition. The instance carries its own world-space transform (position, rotation, scale). Editing the component later automatically updates all its instances. componentId must exist in doc.components. Returns the new instance id in affected. Next: check_assembly finds overlapping, floating and too-thin parts.

componentId.description: Id of an existing Component in doc.components. Obtain via create_component.

position.description: World-space origin [x, y, z] for the instance. Default: [0, 0, 0]. Format [x, y, z]; [x, y] is accepted and placed at z=0.

rotation.description: Euler rotation [rx, ry, rz] in radians (XYZ order). Default: [0, 0, 0].

scale.description: Per-axis scale factors [sx, sy, sz]. Default: [1, 1, 1]. All components must be finite.

name: insert_instance

description: Splice a new feature history step into featureHistory immediately after the step with id afterStepId, then regenerate the document. If afterStepId is omitted the step is appended at the end. The new step is always active (suppressed=false).

afterStepId.description: Id of the existing FeatureStep after which to insert the new step. If omitted, the new step is appended at the end of featureHistory.

label.description: Optional human/AI-readable label for this step, e.g. "Base plate".

name.description: Registry command name (snake_case) for the new step, e.g. "add_box". Must be a known command name; unknown names are stored but skipped during replay.

params.description: Params object for the command named in `name`. Must be compatible with that command.

name: insert_step

description: List the physics model: every rigid body with its computed mass (kg), centre of mass (document units) and moment of inertia about its joint axis (kg·m², revolute joints; a prismatic joint reports translatingMassKg instead: the body plus the bodies it carries) and the densities used (densitySources, densityDefaulted: true when the steel default filled in, with a DYN_DENSITY_DEFAULTED warning; unverified), plus joints, gear couplings, motors, propellers and cylinder pressures, and any problem that would stop simulate_motion. With mobility true (default) it also reports the closed-loop structure: data.topology { tree: spanning-tree joints rooted at the ground, loops: joints that close loops, flipped: tree joints whose declared parent/child sense is reversed }, data.mobility { gruebler: 6·bodies − joint constraints; rank: numerical rank of the loop-constraint Jacobian at the start pose; dof: tree coordinates − rank = true degrees of freedom (a crank-driven slider-crank has 1); redundant: constraint rows that repeat what the tree already fixes (FPR_REDUNDANT_CONSTRAINT, with the joint to change; make one revolute loop joint spherical); treeCoordinates, constraintRows } and data.loopGapsM (distance in metres between the two pins of each loop at the start pose; above 1 µm simulate_motion refuses with FPR_LOOP_OPEN). Gear couplings are not counted in the degrees of freedom. Use it to check a setup before simulating. Read-only; needs no physics engine.

mobility.description: Report data.topology, data.mobility and data.loopGapsM (default true).

name: inspect_dynamics

description: List the faces of an exact 3D solid with located geometry: per face its index (the same index inspect_topology uses), surface type (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, bspline, …), area, centroid, outward unit normal (planes), axis and radius (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus: the torus minor radius; a cone reports its radius at the face centroid) and, on request, sample points inside the trimmed face. With graph=true it also returns the face adjacency graph: per face its surface parameters, whether it is stored reversed, its loops (edge indices, outer loop first) and uv box; per edge the faces it joins and whether the edge is convex, concave, smooth (tangent faces) or unknown. Use it to pick faces for holes, datums, tolerances or meshing: sample points and centroids are positions in the document frame. All lengths are document units and areas their square. Requires the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server); the default Manifold kernel has no B-rep and the command is refused with error.code KRN_NO_EXACT_KERNEL. Does not modify the document.

entityId.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to inspect (a primitive, or a boolean / fillet / chamfer / shell result).

faces.description: 0-based face indices to report (as listed by inspect_topology). Omit to report every face. An index out of range is refused.

graph.description: When true, also return the face adjacency graph (all faces, regardless of the faces filter). Default false.

samples.description: Number of sample points per face, placed inside the trimmed face on a regular uv grid (0-256). Default 0 (none).

name: inspect_faces

description: List the exact B-rep topology of a 3D solid as the geometry kernel holds it: its faces (surface type, area) and its unique edges (curve type, length, start/end/mid points). The edge indices are the ones fillet_edge and chamfer_edge take in edgeIndices — inspect first, then pick edges by position (e.g. the edge whose mid point is at the top front). Works on primitives and on boolean / fillet / chamfer / shell results (they keep their exact construction). Requires the OCC kernel (the desktop default; LLULL_KERNEL=occt-native or occt for the CLI and server); the default Manifold kernel has no B-rep and gracefully no-ops. Does not modify the document.

id.description: Id of the 3D solid entity to inspect.

name: inspect_topology

description: Replay a named recipe's steps ADDITIVELY on top of the current document, assigning fresh entity ids each time. Existing entities are never removed or changed. Each call is independent — instantiating the same recipe twice produces two separate copies, each with their own unique ids. The recipe must already exist (call save_recipe first). The step is recorded in featureHistory so replaying the history re-expands the recipe.

name.description: Name of the recipe to instantiate. Must match an existing recipe created by save_recipe (case-sensitive). Example: "bracket_v1", "wheel_assembly".

name: instantiate_recipe

description: Joint capacity of one placed fastener stack (read-only, V2 hook): single shear = fastener Fsu × π·D²/4 (one shear plane) and, for each sheet layer, bearing = sheet Fbru × D × layer thickness at edge ratio e/D. D is the catalogue nominal diameter; each sheet uses the material assigned to its entity (assign_material); the fastener material is fastenerMaterial. Values come from get_material_allowable with the EXACT basis you give (never substituted). The result basis follows MMPDS rules and is never upgraded: A only if every input is A; B if all are A or B; otherwise "mixed" with the per-input list in data.inputs. Typical / supplier values make the capacities unverified (data.unverified). The capacities are an input to a stress check, not a margin: reviewRequired is always true.

edOverD.description: Edge-distance ratio e/D of the bearing allowable (1.5 or 2.0): the Fbru value is keyed by it.

fastenerBasis.description: Basis of the fastener Fsu value to use (A, B, S, …); no other basis is substituted.

fastenerMaterial.description: Material id of the fastener (record carrying the shear allowable Fsu).

sheetBasis.description: Basis of the sheet Fbru value to use; no other basis is substituted.

sheetDirection.description: Grain direction of the sheet value (L, LT, …); omit for a direction-free value.

stackId.description: Id of a placed stack (fst-…); check_fastener_layout lists them.

name: joint_capacity

description: Report which geometry kernel is active for this session: "occt" (exact B-rep: STEP import, fillets, exact volumes) or "manifold" (mesh booleans only), its OCCT version / build, the optional capabilities it has (topology, analyze, distance, exportStep, importShapes, brepBlobs, ...), the isolation (worker, in-process or process) and, when the exact kernel failed to start, the fallback reason. Also returns the document modelingTolerance (linear mm, angular rad, maxImportTolerance mm) with its source, and warnings KRN_KERNEL_FALLBACK / KRN_KERNEL_MISMATCH (the document was written by another kernel or OCCT version). Call this before relying on exact results.
name: kernel_info
